9DC574E0DFE60131429B68A86D17958E.description: Use social networks and information tools to gather and share information (e.g., social bookmarking, online collaborative tools)

9DC521B0DFE60131429A68A86D17958E.description: Gather and share information and opinions as a result of communication with others (e.g., video/audio chat, interview, podcast, multi-media presentations)

9DC4DD40DFE60131429968A86D17958E.description: While reading, listening, and viewing, evaluate the message for bias, commercialism and hidden agendas (e.g., product placement, television ad, radio ad, movie, body image, sexism)

9DC49420DFE60131429868A86D17958E.description: Engage in activities with learners from a variety of cultures through electronic means (e.g., podcasts, video chats, distance learning)

9DC44630DFE60131429768A86D17958E.description: Practice safe and ethical behaviors when communicating and interacting with others (e.g., safe information to share online, appropriate language use, utilize appropriate sites and materials, respect diverse perspectives)

9DC401E0DFE60131429668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ethical and legal use of information by citing sources using a prescribed format (e.g., citation of information used)

9DC3BBE0DFE60131429568A86D17958E.description: Select and use multiple resources to generate and answer questions and establish validity of information (e.g., print, subscription databases, web resources)

9DC37610DFE60131429468A86D17958E.description: Multiple Literacies: Students will research, summarize, and communicate information in a variety of media and formats (textual, visual, and digital).

9DC32E10DFE60131429368A86D17958E.description: Students will identify, locate, and evaluate information.

9DC29270DFE60131429168A86D17958E.description: Interact and collaborate with others in learning situations by contributing questions, information, opinions, and ideas using a variety of media and formats

9DC23D20DFE60131429068A86D17958E.description: Apply conversation strategies (e.g., listen while others are talking, eye contact, tone, stay on topic, non-verbal cues)

9DC1E8E0DFE60131428F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate sensitivity to the use of words in general as well as to a particular audience (e.g., stereotypes, connotations, subtleties of language)

9DC190E0DFE60131428E68A86D17958E.description: Reciprocal Communication: Students will develop, apply, and adapt reciprocal communication skills.

9DC14DE0DFE60131428D68A86D17958E.description: Listen to, analyze, and evaluate message, purpose, and perspective of information being communicated

9DC0FB80DFE60131428C68A86D17958E.description: Listen and ask probing questions to elicit information

9DC0B570DFE60131428B68A86D17958E.description: Apply listening skills needed for multiple situations and modalities (e.g., video, audio, distance, one-to-one, group)

9DC074A0DFE60131428A68A86D17958E.description: Listening Skills: Students will develop, apply, and refine active listening skills across a variety of situations.

9DC03220DFE60131428968A86D17958E.description: Utilize available media to enhance communication

9DBFE520DFE60131428868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and adjust speaking techniques for a variety of purposes and situations

9DBF5A50DFE60131428768A86D17958E.description: Communicate ideas and information in a manner appropriate for the purpose and setting

9DBF0C60DFE60131428668A86D17958E.description: Speaking Skills: Students will develop and apply speaking skills to communicate key ideas in a variety of situations.

9DBEC820DFE60131428568A86D17958E.description: Students will learn and apply speaking and listening skills and strategies to communicate.

9DBE4060DFE60131428368A86D17958E.description: Analyze models and examples (own and others') of various genres in order to create a similar piece

9DBDFAB0DFE60131428268A86D17958E.description: Select and apply an organizational structure appropriate to the task (e.g., order of importance, similarity and difference, posing and answering a question)

9DBDB300DFE60131428168A86D17958E.description: Write considering typical characteristics of the selected genre (e.g., letter to the editor, report, email, class notes, essay, research paper, play)

9DBD5AE0DFE60131428068A86D17958E.description: Write in a variety of genres, considering audience (e.g., a known or unknown individual, a business, organization, or cyber audience)

9DBD0E30DFE60131427F68A86D17958E.description: Write in a variety of genres, considering purpose (e.g., inform, entertain, persuade, instruct)

9DBCBF20DFE60131427E68A86D17958E.description: Writing Genres: Students will write for a variety of purposes and audiences in multiple genres.

9DBC7D20DFE60131427D68A86D17958E.description: Publish a legible document (e.g., report, podcast, web page, PowerPoint) that applies formatting techniques to aid comprehension (e.g., differing fonts, title page, highlighting, spacing)

9DBC3B20DFE60131427C68A86D17958E.description: Edit writing for format and conventions (e.g., spelling, capitalization, grammar, punctuation)

9DBBE620DFE60131427B68A86D17958E.description: Provide oral, written, and/or electronic feedback to other writers; utilize others' feedback to improve own writing

9DBB9AF0DFE60131427A68A86D17958E.description: Revise to improve writing (e.g., quality of ideas, organization, sentence fluency, word choice, voice)

9DBB5550DFE60131427968A86D17958E.description:
Generate a draft by:
  • Selecting and organizing ideas relevant to topic, purpose, and genre
  • Composing paragraphs with sentences of varying length and complexity avoiding fragments and run-ons
  • Using effective transitional words and cues to unify important ideas

9DBB10F0DFE60131427868A86D17958E.description: Use prewriting activities and inquiry tools, using available technology, to generate and organize information, guide writing and answer questions

9DBAC910DFE60131427768A86D17958E.description: Writing Process: Students will apply the writing process to plan, draft, revise, edit and publish writing using correct spelling, grammar, punctuation, and other standard conventions appropriate for grade level.

9DBA8060DFE60131427668A86D17958E.description: Students will learn and apply writing skills and strategies to communicate.

9DB9C0C0DFE60131427468A86D17958E.description: Respond to text verbally, in writing, or artistically

9DB98240DFE60131427368A86D17958E.description: Use examples and details to make inferences or logical predictions while previewing and reading text

9DB943D0DFE60131427268A86D17958E.description: Self-monitor comprehension for accuracy and understanding when errors detract from meaning by applying appropriate strategies to self-correct

9DB903C0DFE60131427168A86D17958E.description: Build and activate prior knowledge in order to clarify text, deepen understanding, and make connections while reading

9DB8BFA0DFE60131427068A86D17958E.description: Select text for a particular purpose (e.g., understand, interpret, enjoy, solve problems, form an opinion, answer a specific question, discover models for own writing)

9DB86F00DFE60131426F68A86D17958E.description: Generate and/or answer literal, inferential, critical, and interpretive questions, analyzing prior knowledge, information from the text and additional sources, to support answers

9DB823D0DFE60131426E68A86D17958E.description: Use narrative and informational text to develop a national and global multi-cultural perspective

9DB7DF80DFE60131426D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the social, historical, cultural, and biographical influences in a variety of genres

9DB791C0DFE60131426C68A86D17958E.description: Explain and make inferences based on the characteristics of narrative and informational genres (e.g., textbooks, myths, fantasies, science fiction, drama, periodicals, essays)

9DB74FC0DFE60131426B68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of text features to locate information and gain meaning from a text (e.g., index, annotations, maps, charts, tables, graphs, headings, subheadings)

9DB70CC0DFE60131426A68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of organizational patterns found in informational text (e.g., sequence, description, cause and effect, compare/contrast, fact/opinion, proposition/support)

9DB6C3B0DFE60131426968A86D17958E.description: Summarize, analyze, and synthesize informational text using main idea and supporting details

9DB67020DFE60131426868A86D17958E.description: Analyze author's use of literary devices (e.g., foreshadowing, personification, idiom, oxymoron, hyperbole, flashback, suspense, symbolism, irony)

9DB628E0DFE60131426768A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze elements of narrative text (e.g., character development, setting, plot development, conflict, point of view, theme

9DB5DC90DFE60131426668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the meaning, reliability, and validity of the text considering author's purpose, and perspective

9DB58C30DFE60131426568A86D17958E.description: Comprehension: Students will extract and construct meaning using prior knowledge, applying text information, and monitoring comprehension while reading grade level text.

9DB53E60DFE60131426468A86D17958E.description: Determine meaning using print and digital reference materials

9DB4E7D0DFE60131426368A86D17958E.description: Analyze semantic relationships (e.g., figurative language, connotations, subtle distinctions)

9DB49420DFE60131426268A86D17958E.description: Select and apply knowledge of context clues (e.g., word, phrase, sentence, and paragraph clues, re-reading) and text features (e.g., glossary, headings, subheadings, index, tables, maps, graphs, charts) appropriate to a particular text to determine meaning of unknown words

9DB44610DFE60131426168A86D17958E.description: Relate new grade level vocabulary to prior knowledge and use in new situations.

9DB3FD30DFE60131426068A86D17958E.description: Determine meaning of words through structural analysis, using knowledge of Greek, Latin, and Anglo-Saxon roots, prefixes, and suffixes to understand complex words, including words in science, mathematics, and social studies

9DB3B010DFE60131425F68A86D17958E.description: Vocabulary: Students will build literary, general academic, and content specific grade level vocabulary.

9DB36D40DFE60131425E68A86D17958E.description: Adjust oral or silent reading pace based on purpose, text difficulty, form, and style

9DB31C90DFE60131425D68A86D17958E.description: Apply elements of prosodic reading to a group of related texts and explore their potential for performance

9DB2CEF0DFE60131425C68A86D17958E.description: Fluency: Students will read a variety of grade level texts fluently with accuracy, appropriate pace, phrasing, and expression.

9DB284E0DFE60131425B68A86D17958E.description: Word Analysis: Concept mastered at a previous grade level

9DB23E40DFE60131425A68A86D17958E.description: Phonological Awareness: Concept mastered at a previous grade level

9DB1FAF0DFE60131425968A86D17958E.description: Knowledge of Print: Concept mastered at a previous grade level

9DB1BB70DFE60131425868A86D17958E.description: Students will learn and apply reading skills and strategies to comprehend text.

Generate a draft by:

  • Composing paragraphs with simple, compound, and complex sentences, avoiding fragments and run-ons of varying length and complexity
  • Concluding with detailed summary linked to the purpose of the composition

9D918230DFE60131422868A86D17958E.description: Use narrative and informational text to develop a national and global multi-cultural perspective

9D905450DFE60131422468A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of organizational patterns found in informational text (e.g., sequence, description, cause and effect, compare/contrast, fact/opinion)

9D900FE0DFE60131422368A86D17958E.description: Summarize, analyze, and synthesize informational text using main idea and supporting details

9D8FB2A0DFE60131422268A86D17958E.description: Interpret and explain the author's use of literary devices (e.g., simile, metaphor, alliteration, onomatopoeia, imagery, rhythm)

9D8F48E0DFE60131422168A86D17958E.description: Summarize narrative text using understanding of characters, setting, sequence of events, plot, and theme

9D8F0450DFE60131422068A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze elements of narrative text (e.g., character development, setting, plot development, conflict, point of view, theme)

9D8EC560DFE60131421F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how author's purpose and perspective affect the meaning and reliability of the text

9D8E8570DFE60131421E68A86D17958E.description: Comprehension: Students will extract and construct meaning using prior knowledge, applying text information, and monitoring comprehension while reading grade level text.

9D8E03A0DFE60131421C68A86D17958E.description: Identify semantic relationships (e.g., metaphors, similes, idioms, analogies, comparisons)

9D8DB730DFE60131421B68A86D17958E.description: Select and apply knowledge of context clues (e.g., word, phrase, sentence, and paragraph clues, re-reading) and text features (e.g., glossary, headings, subheadings, index, tables, maps, charts) to determine meaning of unknown words in a variety of text structures

9D8CEEC0DFE60131421868A86D17958E.description: Vocabulary: Students will build literary, general academic, and content specific grade level vocabulary.

9D8CAAE0DFE60131421768A86D17958E.description: Adjust oral or silent reading pace based on purpose, text difficulty, form, and style

9D8C16B0DFE60131421568A86D17958E.description: Fluency: Students will read a variety of grade level texts fluently with accuracy, appropriate pace, phrasing, and expression.

9D8BCB20DFE60131421468A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of phonetic and structural analysis (e.g., Anglo-Saxon, Greek, and Latin roots, foreign words frequently used in English, bases, affixes)

9D8B8660DFE60131421368A86D17958E.description: Word Analysis: Students will use knowledge of phonetic and structural analysis to read, write, and spell grade level text.

9D8B4240DFE60131421268A86D17958E.description: Phonological Awareness: Concept mastered at a previous grade level

9D8B0020DFE60131421168A86D17958E.description: Knowledge of Print: Concept mastered at a previous grade level

9D8AB9C0DFE60131421068A86D17958E.description: Students will learn and apply reading skills and strategies to comprehend text.

A29A4DD0DFE60131496A68A86D17958E.description: Identify how Earth materials are used (fuels, building materials, sustaining plant life)

A293BAC0DFE60131495368A86D17958E.description: Identify how parts of plants and animals function to meet basic needs (e.g., leg of an insect helps an insect move, root of a plant helps the plant obtain water)

A28FFE00DFE60131494668A86D17958E.description: Describe magnetic behavior in terms of attraction and repulsion

A28E64B0DFE60131494068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate metric measurements to describe physical properties

A28D8880DFE60131493D68A86D17958E.description: Students will explore and describe the physical properties of matter and its changes

A28C90B0DFE60131493A68A86D17958E.description: Communicate the problem, design, and solution

A28A8470DFE60131493368A86D17958E.description: Recognize many different people study science

comments: Students will combine scientific processes and knowledge with scientific reasoning and critical thinking to ask questions about phenomena and propose explanations based on gathered evidence.

9F030A40DFE60131447068A86D17958E.description: Identify state leaders and the impact of their decisions that effect public policy

9EFF7170DFE60131446568A86D17958E.description: Students will identify and explain the foundation, structure, and function of Nebraska's government.

9EFEC740DFE60131446368A86D17958E.description: Students will develop and apply the skills of civic responsibility to make informed decisions based upon knowledge of government at local, state, national and international levels.

document.title: Nebraska English Language Arts Standards

F15F26E83A654325A91CD5BA9A29D258.description: Use appropriate digital tools (e.g., social media, online collaborative tools, apps) to communicate with others for conveying information, gathering opinions, and solving problems.

3E1A25310D674B7FB6AB2F68AE45AF7D.description: Practice safe and ethical behaviors when communicating and interacting with others digitally (e.g., safe information to share, appropriate language use, utilize appropriate sites and materials, respect diverse perspectives).

B12C2739BA324BE49AA1FAD6638C2110.description: Digital Citizenship: Students will practice the norms of appropriate and responsible technology use.

87F91326ADE949159CA5D5AB49E7E5F2.description: Use or decipher multiple formats of print and digital text (e.g., cursive, manuscript, font, graphics, symbols).

7C888457CA8C4D7F8F640FF2B0157BCF.description: Demonstrate ethical use of information and copyright guidelines by appropriately quoting or paraphrasing from a text and citing the source using available resources (e.g., online citation tools).

7E3A539E831E475D98E23BE6B5234415.description: Locate, organize, analyze, and evaluate information from print and digital resources to generate and answer questions and create new understandings.

6B60EA5796C94D34B7ACAE322707180A.description: Information Fluency: Students will evaluate, create, and communicate information in a variety of media and formats (textual, visual, and digital).

86DD18905D6D410FADB91A3BCED1F6CA.description: Multiple Literacies: Students will apply information fluency and practice digital citizenship.

35CEBA943E3849AABBA7E82AB71C3CE5.description: Collaboratively converse with peers and adults on grade-appropriate topics and texts, building on others' ideas to clearly express one's own views while respecting diverse perspectives.

33D0681652454776BF0831E9ABD413C6.description: Listen, ask clarifying questions, summarize, and explain information being communicated and consider its contribution to a topic, text, or issue under study.

5489A5D1BB1D4B2B8B0A177B399EC11F.description: Apply conversation strategies to recognize and consider new information presented by others in relationship to one's own ideas.

70EFF96F10BC4C82A1328D28852E578E.description: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., stereotypes, multiple meanings of words) in conversation.

259A04822372444298A251755B388CFF.description: Demonstrate appropriate social etiquette and apply social cues when communicating.

51AEE5AB57EE44B892641B3EA75BE543.description: Reciprocal Communication: Students will develop, apply, and adapt reciprocal communication skills.

EE2D97974D544621B74347DFCA99D6FA.description: Complete a task following multi-step directions.

470851A740F04BA6B05EC39553892C4E.description: Identify the purpose and credibility of information being presented in diverse media and formats.

05BB1AE7E09C43358B52737E59A74346.description: Demonstrate active and attentive listening skills (e.g., eye contact, nonverbal cues, recalling, questioning) for multiple situations and modalities.

6DD721240D324920A01DAE5553D8CECB.description: Listening: Students will develop and demonstrate active listening skills across a variety of situations.

F8E75D1CD5B94403B274C9336452A79E.description: Ask pertinent questions to acquire or confirm information.

2D194D6AACB449BEAB7F7A5F41815FC8.description: Convey a perspective with clear reasoning and support.

DCA99E98A1724B569DF30183F13D9697.description: Utilize appropriate visual and/or digital tools to enhance verbal communication and add interest.

D3681B36955E40899D23F0457D5FAD3B.description: Demonstrate appropriate speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, clear pronunciation, word choice) for a variety of purposes and situations, including interpreting text.

EBCD02718FBF4DE7B76537DC847C0272.description: Communicate ideas and information in a clear and concise manner suited to the purpose, setting, and audience (formal voice or informal voice), using appropriate word choice, grammar, and sentence structure.

8C8C2D1F85784577BB8CC92EE48F37A8.description: Speaking: Students will develop, apply, and refine speaking skills and strategies to communicate key ideas in a variety of situations.

8CC9891A8AD54D298BC06AF7A970163C.description: Speaking and Listening: Students will develop and apply speaking and listening skills and strategies to communicate for a variety of purposes.

1086A4E074D643D084F4D45DBFE75D01.description: Compare various mentor texts and/or exemplars to create a similar piece.

CF5C823924F442E6B3350EF6BDF67C42.description: Use precise word choice and domain-specific vocabulary to write in a variety of modes.

9E29815AC10645D498430F9AA3679432.description: Conduct and publish research projects to answer questions or solve problems using multiple resources to support theses.

937609E61A1A4D449D20896F8453418F.description: Provide evidence from literary or informational text to support analysis, reflection, and research.

9747B636D5DA4A9E99ED2A5B528DFD20.description: Communicate information and ideas effectively in analytic, descriptive, informative, narrative, poetic, persuasive, and reflective modes to multiple audiences using a variety of media and formats.

6CC98DAE620F45A3A57DFC5342EC1C80.description: Writing Modes: Student will write in multiple modes for a variety of purposes and audiences across disciplines.

1EC99E8A25DD4D2B89A7E1290E86184F.description: Publish a legible document in manuscript, cursive, or digital format, and apply formatting techniques (e.g., indenting paragraphs, title).

BB24FA22C25C4C9F815F648C68690D83.description: Display academic honesty and integrity by avoiding plagiarism and/or overreliance on any one source and by following a standard format for citation.

358092B2E7F14F4D86E615BA37917687.description: Proofread and edit writing recursively for format and conventions of standard English (e.g., spelling, capitalization, grammar, punctuation, syntax, semantics).

46E324F90E94489F87C24E2FC33340A4.description: Adjust writing processes to persevere in short and long-term writing tasks of increasing length and complexity.

618914499D244A449F43FEB6D0DCBB0D.description: Provide oral, written, and/or digital descriptive feedback to other writers.

A397F23589204E53A34F4C50752DC7D9.description: Revise to improve and clarify writing through self-monitoring strategies and feedback from others.

CFC920FF123E440FBFA79C7DE389FCC2.description: Compose paragraphs with grammatically correct sentences of varying length, complexity, and type.

B4962C41EDE94AC8A567493AB72E6F0C.description: Gather and use relevant information and evidence from multiple authoritative print and/or digital sources to support claims or theses.

B9AD99886C75434A975BBB1535D70AA5.description: Generate a draft that develops a clear topic suited to the purpose and intended audience and organizational pattern, including a clear introduction, body, and conclusion with appropriate transitions.

7E8060756FC74D65BBEFDCD6CC66C89A.description: Use prewriting activities and inquiry tools to generate ideas, organize information, guide writing, and answer questions.

FF1F6D004A32414D82503D06A12C00D3.description: Writing Process: Students will apply the writing process to plan, draft, revise, edit, and publish writing using correct spelling, grammar, punctuation, and other conventions of standard English appropriate for grade-level.

AFBDE1FCC31A4FB5B33E34453DD20FAB.description: Writing: Students will learn and apply writing skills and strategies to communicate.

62806FE577504E238F6D96847BC5BA38.description: Compare and contrast the text of a story, drama, or poem and a visual or oral presentation of the text.

DD5278334E3C4050B1EF933395FFED57.description: Demonstrate an understanding of text via multiple mediums (e.g., writing, artistic representation, video, other media).

EDDEFB1128DB4072993EA93E1F274461.description: Make and confirm/modify predictions and inferences before, during, and after reading literary, informational, digital text, and/or media.

90ACBE08867D4099A37335B76E1AEB18.description: Self-monitor comprehension by recognizing when meaning is disrupted and apply strategies to clarify, confirm, or correct.

0546163D0F624253B111B3EB62310B43.description: Build background knowledge and activate prior knowledge to identify text-to-self, text-to-text, and text-to-world connections before, during, and after reading.

9F692FE1CCF847388AA5F91687DA9C7C.description: Select text and explain the purpose (e.g., answer a question, solve problems, enjoy, form an opinion, understand a specific viewpoint, predict outcomes, discover models for own writing, accomplish a task).

47019F476B4D45F09F6963094AEAFD76.description: Identify and apply knowledge of organizational patterns to comprehend informational text (e.g., sequence, description, cause and effect, compare/contrast, fact/opinion).

D530C93D6FF445D794675B982F349069.description: Construct and/or answer literal, inferential, and critical questions and support answers with explicit evidence from the text or additional sources.

94687CAA0C8A40DFA03ABEA06B661710.description: Compare and contrast similar themes, topics, and/or patterns of events in literary and informational texts to develop a multicultural perspective.

8FF427D6B6114532824A1B8B1FAA2F7A.description: Compare and contrast the characteristics that distinguish a variety of literary and informational texts.

F8B834F062294F3AA305A697FFDB59C8.description: Use text features to locate information and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of print and digital text.

4082FF8C5B9E432A911DC5AC84892B01.description: Determine main ideas and supporting details from informational text and/or media.

0A1161C0F3214D9A9211110F04C9BB13.description: Summarize a literary text and/or media, using key details to identify the theme.

3E2959AA30044C76A7BA7D6F4976696F.description: Identify and explain why authors use literary devices (e.g., simile, metaphor, alliteration, onomatopoeia, imagery, rhythm, personification, hyperbole, idioms).

CAA75B129FFA49D3A091900CAEBC07F9.description: Identify and describe elements of literary text (e.g., characters, setting, plot, point of view, theme).

5664A013797D49C08C0AE4C6D2D6FD34.description: Examine text to determine author's purpose(s) and describe how author's perspective (e.g., beliefs, assumptions, biases) influences text.

AE9BAA9756CE4FE6A8D17C61A0A95593.description: Comprehension: Students will construct meaning by using prior knowledge and text information while reading grade-level literary and informational text.

EC0B3EC1FC92404B881F1CF828F21F22.description: Identify semantic relationships (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs, homophones, multiple-meaning words) to determine the meaning of words, aid in comprehension, and improve writing.

51F948E56B8846F69E5C8669615EC5DB.description: Acquire new academic and content-specific grade-level vocabulary, relate to prior knowledge, and apply in new situations.

D139A9C77C114A8C93E4942C5E9DF6CD.description: Apply context clues (e.g., word, phrase, and sentence, and paragraph clues) and text features to infer meaning of unknown words.

DACBBBEE9E22497EAA721A90209E5E61.description: Apply knowledge of word structure elements, known words, and word patterns to determine meaning (e.g., plurals, possessives, parts of speech, affixes, base and root words).

A3593546E2964034A2EE6B651DB63161.description: Vocabulary: Students will build and use conversational, academic, and content-specific grade-level vocabulary.

483330ABD7CB497982BF4C0F13E8C1DE.description: Use context to adjust pace and prosody based on purpose, text complexity, form, and style.

A2420A058FAE40FCAFEB3AA8B02863DD.description: Listen to and read text of increasing length and/or complexity to increase reader stamina.

EF24D8E90AA7421F83C9EB816DCFCC67.description: Fluency: Students will develop accuracy, phrasing, and expression while reading a variety of grade-level print/digital text to support comprehension.

F19FDBFBC9F04119948D240DECC48B35.description: Use word structure to read text (e.g., prefixes/suffixes, syllabication, derivation).

14E60F621021417E8EA186658FA65BDD.description: Know and apply advanced sound/spelling patterns (e.g., Anglo-Saxon common roots and affixes, vowel variance, multi-syllable words) when reading, writing, and spelling grade-level text.

2B2F706F9AC54C00880A144AD3D638FB.description: Word Analysis: Students will use phonetic analysis to read and write grade-level text.

35920636AC6B48AD97F47C37F49EBAA0.description: Phonological Awareness: Students will demonstrate phonological awareness through oral activities.
comments: Mastered in Grade 1 and blended with other skills at this grade level.

F23754EE28CA44E6BD6EA7ED6C918E99.description: Concepts of Print: Students will demonstrate knowledge of the concepts of print.
comments: Mastered in Grade 1 and blended with other skills at this grade level.

64E92CB4331D47B99B61903F5D08AB96.description: Reading: Students will learn and apply reading skills and strategies to comprehend text.

document.title: Nebraska Social Studies Standards

9F4C1850DFE60131452268A86D17958E.description: Present historical information about the United States (e.g., pictures, posters, oral/written narratives, and electronic presentations)

9F4BB950DFE60131452168A86D17958E.description: Gather historical information about the United States (e.g., document archives, newspapers, interviews)

9F4B50E0DFE60131452068A86D17958E.description: Identify, obtain, and cite appropriate sources for research about Early U.S. History, incorporating primary and secondary sources (e.g., Cite sources using a prescribed format)

9F4AFDD0DFE60131451F68A86D17958E.description: Develop questions about United States history

9F4AB610DFE60131451E68A86D17958E.description: Students will develop historical research skills.

9F4A10E0DFE60131451C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationships among historical events in the United States and the students' lives today (i.e., current events)

9F49AF10DFE60131451B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the cause and effect relationships among key events in history (e.g., Revolutionary War, founding of the United States)

9F494720DFE60131451A68A86D17958E.description: Identify how decisions affected events in the United States (e.g., secession of the American Colonies from Britain)

9F490010DFE60131451968A86D17958E.description: Examine alternative courses of action in United States history (e.g., What were the causes of the American Revolution?)

9F48B420DFE60131451868A86D17958E.description: Analyze sources on Early American History through determination of credibility, contextualization, and corroboration

9F4854D0DFE60131451768A86D17958E.description: Students will analyze past and current events, issues, and problems.

9F47B080DFE60131451568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast primary and secondary sources to better understand multiple perspectives of the same event (e.g., Court records of the Boston Massacre, The Declaration of Independence, The Constitution, historical biographies, oral histories)

9F476240DFE60131451468A86D17958E.description: Describe how multiple perspectives facilitate the understanding of the full story of US history (e.g., The events surrounding the Boston Massacre, Indian Removal)

9F4719B0DFE60131451368A86D17958E.description: Students will describe and explain multiple perspectives of historical events.

9F4673A0DFE60131451168A86D17958E.description: Describe the appropriate uses of primary and secondary sources

9F4625C0DFE60131451068A86D17958E.description: Describe how the United States and its neighbors in the Western Hemisphere have changed over the course of time using maps, documents, and other artifacts

9F45C3F0DFE60131450F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the impact of people, events, ideas, and symbols, including various cultures and ethnic groups, by era (e.g., Early America/Exploration: American Indian empires in Mesoamerica, the Southwest, and the Mississippi Valley, Coronado, DeSoto, LaSalle; Colonization and Rise of Democratic Institutions: Spanish Missions, French and Indian War: Chief Pontiac; Establishing a Nation: Revolutionary War; Founders and Founding Documents: unique nature of the creation and organization of the American Government, the United States as an exceptional nation based upon personal freedom, the inherent nature of citizens' rights, and democratic ideals, Benjamin Franklin, Thomas Jefferson, and other historical figures, patriotism, national symbols)

9F455050DFE60131450E68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the impact of people, events, ideas, and symbols upon US history using multiple types of sources.

9F44B170DFE60131450C68A86D17958E.description: Examine the chronology of historical events in the United States and their impact on the past, present, and future

9F446B30DFE60131450B68A86D17958E.description: Select and record key national events in chronological order (e.g., timelines)

9F442270DFE60131450A68A86D17958E.description: Describe concepts of time and chronology (e.g., BC, BCE, AD, CE and eras)

9F43D700DFE60131450968A86D17958E.description: Students will examine chronological relationships and patterns, and describe the connections among them.

9F432DD0DFE60131450768A86D17958E.description: Students will develop and apply historical knowledge and skills to research, analyze, and understand key concepts of past, current, and potential issues and events at the local, state, national, and international levels.

9F42CC70DFE60131450668A86D17958E.description: Analyze aspects of human and physical geography that have shaped the settlement and development of Early America, latitude and longitude in the role of early navigation (e.g., groundwater and irrigation, westward expansion of European immigrants, seeds, fertile soils, agriculture, transportation systems, water power)

9F428340DFE60131450568A86D17958E.description: Explain the influences of physical and human geographic features on historical events in the United States (e.g., railroads building along river valley floodplains, building the Erie Canal to connect the East Coast with the Great Lakes, migrating through the Cumberland Gap into the Kentucky bluegrass region)

9F423F30DFE60131450468A86D17958E.description: Students will use geographic skills to interpret issues and events.

9F41FB50DFE60131450368A86D17958E.description: Application of Geography to Issues and Events

9F41B650DFE60131450268A86D17958E.description: Describe human adaptations to the physical environment. (e.g., use of air conditioning, irrigation, agricultural activities, soil testing, erosion control)

9F416F10DFE60131450168A86D17958E.description: Examine patterns of resource distribution and utilization in Early America (e.g., fisheries, forests, agricultural development, early manufacturing regions)

9F4118E0DFE60131450068A86D17958E.description: Analyze issues related to the natural setting in Early America (e.g., access to water, construction materials, and raw materials for daily living and economic development; impact of climate and terrain on living conditions and movement of people goods and services)

9F40CF60DFE6013144FF68A86D17958E.description: Describe how humans have utilized natural resources in the United States (e.g., construction of dams, Transcontinental RR, Erie Canal, National Road, land use changes from prairie and forests to agriculture and ranching)

9F408440DFE6013144FE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of extreme natural events in Early United States History on the human and physical environment (e.g., blizzards, floods, drought)

9F403870DFE6013144FD68A86D17958E.description: Students will describe how humans have adapted to and modified different environments in Early American history.

9F3F6FB0DFE6013144FB68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast historical and present day migrations to and within the United States

9F3F0FB0DFE6013144FA68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast population characteristics of the United States (e.g., density, distribution, growth rates)

9F3EC6E0DFE6013144F968A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast patterns of culture within the United States (e.g., language, religion, food)

9F3E7DD0DFE6013144F868A86D17958E.description: Students will compare, contrast and draw conclusions about the characteristics of culture and migration in the United States.

9F3DEB50DFE6013144F668A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of ecosystems located in the United States (e.g., forests, deserts, grasslands)

9F3D9BB0DFE6013144F568A86D17958E.description: Explain how physical processes shape the United States' features and patterns (e.g., weathering, erosion, plate tectonics and internal forces and climate)

9F3D42C0DFE6013144F468A86D17958E.description: Students will draw conclusions about the natural processes in the physical world.

9F3CB1B0DFE6013144F268A86D17958E.description: Identify and classify regions (e.g., cities, states, and congressional districts)

9F3C6790DFE6013144F168A86D17958E.description: Classify regions and places within the United States using physical and human features (e.g., Rocky Mountains, The Southwest, Great Plains, Corn Belt, Cotton Belt)

9F3C1E50DFE6013144F068A86D17958E.description: Define regions within the United States using multiple criteria. (e.g., Silicon Valley, Bread Basket)

9F3BC8B0DFE6013144EF68A86D17958E.description: Students will compare the characteristics of places and regions and draw conclusions on their impact on human decisions.

9F3B1360DFE6013144ED68A86D17958E.description: Analyze why things are located where they are in the United States (e.g., Why were the 13 colonies located on the eastern side of the United States? Why was corn raised in Pennsylvania and Ohio and cotton in Virginia and Georgia?)

9F3ACD10DFE6013144EC68A86D17958E.description: Apply map skills to analyze physical/political maps of the United States (e.g., identify latitude longitude, and the global grid and identify the location and purpose of time zones)

9F3A7FB0DFE6013144EB68A86D17958E.description: Name and locate major human and physical features in the United States (e.g., states, capitals, and major cities in the United States, Rocky Mountains, Appalachian Mountains, Great Lakes)

9F3A19E0DFE6013144EA68A86D17958E.description: Students will explore where (spatial) and why people, places and environments are organized in the United States.

9F3976E0DFE6013144E868A86D17958E.description: Students will develop and apply spatial perspective and geographic skills to make informed decisions regarding issues and current events at local, state, national and international levels.

9F392F90DFE6013144E768A86D17958E.description: Investigate and report on entrepreneurs and inventors

9F38E6D0DFE6013144E668A86D17958E.description: Investigate Early United States specialization and trade (e.g., fur, tobacco, cotton, lumber)

9F389CD0DFE6013144E568A86D17958E.description: Students will explain how specialization, division of labor, and technology increases productivity and interdependence.

9F372620DFE6013144E068A86D17958E.description: Identify goods and services funded through federal taxes (e.g., armed forces, courts, parks)

9F36E010DFE6013144DF68A86D17958E.description: Students will understand what goods and services the national government provides.

9F3626E0DFE6013144DD68A86D17958E.description: Explain/explore how various financial services are provided by local financial institutions

9F35D510DFE6013144DC68A86D17958E.description: Students will summarize characteristics of financial institutions.

9F354AC0DFE6013144DA68A86D17958E.description: Identify rules and laws that protect and support consumers (e.g., private property, contracts, agreements, and product safety)

9F3501F0DFE6013144D968A86D17958E.description: Identify the importance of financial institutions to households and businesses (e.g., loans to agriculture, business, and individuals in order to provide capital)

9F349E30DFE6013144D868A86D17958E.description: Identify the functions and characteristics of money (e.g., store value, medium of exchange, unit of accounting)

9F3440B0DFE6013144D768A86D17958E.description: Students will summarize characteristics of economic institutions in the United States.

9F33B840DFE6013144D568A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how additional education/training improves productivity and increases standard of living (e.g., apprentice, journeyman, master electrician)

9F337180DFE6013144D468A86D17958E.description: Students will make observations about how human capital can be improved by education, training, and standard of living.

9F332A40DFE6013144D368A86D17958E.description: Describe how competition among sellers results in lower costs and prices, higher product quality, and better customer service

9F32E170DFE6013144D268A86D17958E.description: Students will analyze various markets where buyers and sellers exchange goods or services.

9F324310DFE6013144D068A86D17958E.description: Students will utilize economic reasoning skills to make informed judgments and become effective participants in the economy at the local, state, national and international levels.

9F31FA80DFE6013144CF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the roles and influences of individuals, groups, and the media on governments (e.g., George Washington, John Adams, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Franklin)

9F31AA20DFE6013144CE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how cooperation and conflict among people have contributed to political, economic, and social events and situations in the United States

9F3152D0DFE6013144CD68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of group and individual actions that illustrate civic ideas in the founding of the United States (e.g., freedom, rule of law, equality, civility, cooperation, respect)

9F30FB90DFE6013144CC68A86D17958E.description: Describe the significance of patriotic symbols, songs and activities (e.g., Pledge of Allegiance, "The Star Spangled Banner", "America", commemorating state and national holidays)

9F309D20DFE6013144CB68A86D17958E.description: Explain the constitutional rights and civic responsibilities of U.S. citizens (e.g., freedom of speech, voting, staying informed of issues, respecting the rights, opinions, and beliefs of others, joining a civic group)

9F305440DFE6013144CA68A86D17958E.description: Students will apply democratic principles that are the foundation of the United States government systems to daily life.

9F2FAC80DFE6013144C868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast tribal forms of government, British monarchy, and early American colonial governments

9F2F6000DFE6013144C768A86D17958E.description: Identify the principles of the American Republic (e.g., liberty, democracy, United States Constitution, Bill of Rights)

9F2F0B90DFE6013144C668A86D17958E.description: Describe how the decisions of the national government affect local and state government

9F2EA230DFE6013144C568A86D17958E.description: Describe how colonial and new states' governments laws affected groups within their population (e.g., citizens, slaves, immigrants, women, class systems, tribes)

9F2E5DF0DFE6013144C468A86D17958E.description: Explain the origins, structure, and functions of the three branches of the United States government

9F2E1760DFE6013144C368A86D17958E.description: Explain the historical foundation that led to the formation of the United States constitutional government (e.g., early state constitutions, Declaration of Independence, and the Articles of Confederation)

9F2DD090DFE6013144C268A86D17958E.description: Students will describe the foundation, structure, and function of the United States government.

9F2D3040DFE6013144C068A86D17958E.description: Students will develop and apply the skills of civic responsibility to make informed decisions based upon knowledge of government at local, state, national and international levels.

document.title: Nebraska English Language Arts Standards

6349C6B511084B0A906238C0F1595600.description: Use appropriate digital tools (e.g., social media, online collaborative tools, apps) to communicate with others for conveying information, gathering opinions, and solving problems.

F9294EA15A4E424BB0FB7B84BAB26CA9.description: Practice safe and ethical behaviors when communicating and interacting with others digitally (e.g., safe information to share, appropriate language use, utilize appropriate sites and materials, respect diverse perspectives).

51F93B87228542DCA3BAFB7980F0E9DE.description: Digital Citizenship: Students will practice the norms of appropriate and responsible technology use.

83A7AFDF6DD04B58B2161FDDF2C74859.description: Use or decipher multiple formats of print and digital text (e.g., cursive, manuscript, font, graphics, symbols).

109B79C0A97E475FAC62B153A0E3A6C0.description: Demonstrate ethical use of information and copyright guidelines by appropriately quoting or paraphrasing from a text and citing the source using available resources (e.g., online citation tools, publication guidelines).

7565CC2CD7394FC1AC1EBBAEBA83DF7D.description: Locate, organize, analyze, evaluate, and synthesize information from print and digital resources to create new understandings and defend conclusions.

3C39E55A98FE40EDB107BFB0D98F61B1.description: Information Fluency: Students will evaluate, create, and communicate information in a variety of media and formats (textual, visual, and digital).

CEB9567E79F34E88A2F30C73758C45B1.description: Multiple Literacies: Students will apply information fluency and practice digital citizenship.

C1355E4C0A714E8D9BE36D78770BB6B6.description: Collaboratively converse with peers and adults on grade-appropriate topics and texts, building on others' ideas to clearly and persuasively express one's own views while respecting diverse perspectives.
