A275CB860A394683899932A942451A86.description: Measurement: Students will perform and compare measurements and apply formulas.

EFB8139458904B14B1B0903437A74219.description: No additional indicator(s) at this level. Mastery is expected at previous grade levels.

E39847FD308B4FA885EA97A6BF95120D.description: Coordinate Geometry: Students will determine location, orientation, and relationships on the coordinate plane.

E72FF54BE7A94E78991D0D951D139A8A.description: Recognize and draw lines of symmetry in two-dimensional shapes.

4334397478204045BCDC7567E31DB068.description: Sketch angles of a specified measure.

743E02AD5C0E479DA0F5253D44747C56.description: Measure angles in whole number degrees using a protractor.

B6AD2B1AC382451796886B1733739460.description: Classify two-dimensional shapes based on the presence or absence of parallel and perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of specific angles.

A34ECBB5EA054F5B92461E8A7D3049F9.description: Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles, parallel lines, perpendicular lines, and intersecting lines, and recognize them in two-dimensional figures.

7A9D98252A6640B0AED6BCD4AEB7F6C1.description: Classify an angle as acute, obtuse, or right.

BF5F2DF863DF427DAA2C5D61A98E5B8B.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed where two rays share a common endpoint.

68B7CAC4CC6542C891FA37DC24B79541.description: Characteristics: Students will identify and describe geometric characteristics and create two- and three-dimensional shapes.

D2D21E283BC2437B9CA6942A854E1EFF.description: Geometry: Students will communicate geometric concepts and measurement concepts using multiple representations to reason, solve problems, and make connections within mathematics and across disciplines.

C54BDECF61574206B7F2722044ACCB06.description: Solve real-world problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.

4B28527414894809BC422CCF61AD841C.description: Solve real-world problems involving multi-step equations comprised of whole numbers using the four operations, including interpreting remainders.

D135C4D5B283408DBC71FF01023E9554.description: Applications: Students will solve real-world problems involving equations with fractions.

50BA60091F684D5EAA6A60E9C33C576A.description: Solve one- and two-step problems which use any or all of the four basic operations and include the use of a letter to represent the unknown quantity.

593B55701ACE433A921BE7A6606567B9.description: Algebraic Processes: Students will apply the operational properties when evaluating expressions and solving equations.

E7AC8510CAE243ECB05B1A1014E2FC92.description: Generate and analyze a number or shape pattern to follow a given rule, such as y = 3x + 5 is a rule to describe a relationship between two variables and can be used to find a second number when a first number is given.

D4738E61489748FAB2EFDA704C6D9221.description: Create a simple algebraic expression or equation using a variable for an unknown number to represent a math process (e.g., 3 + n = 15, 81 ÷ n = 9).

F0567929C8A74C58A7FD851672B126B3.description: Algebraic Relationships: Students will demonstrate, represent, and show relationships with expressions and equations.

D8F023D6BD9944F9902A26CCE5D603EA.description: Algebra: Students will communicate algebraic concepts using multiple representations to reason, solve problems, and make connections within mathematics and across disciplines.

70060D1382A84DF88E36F0A1E5557FBA.description: Determine the reasonableness of whole number products and quotients in real-world problems using estimation, compatible numbers, mental computations, or other strategies.

A118A55EA36D4975A6CDCBB8128E2A4F.description: Multiply a fraction by a whole number.

EC22967AEFB9401EBB719F2EE345A770.description: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.

9A5CCDA796234A47AF4CB5EC57D52557.description: Use drawings, words, and symbols to explain the meaning of addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators.

28DB5C8333654DA1BEFA480AD17AA9F4.description: Divide up to a four-digit whole number by a one-digit divisor with and without a remainder.

2583B8C13E8049D5A7EABF52643DAED2.description: Multiply a two-digit whole number by a two-digit whole number using the standard algorithm.

381A66807A704BCDB0B903BE53942C86.description: Multiply a four-digit whole number by a one-digit whole number.

D2DA0747AC9F4C01A912392018BD3FEC.description: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

88484AE6539447D2A52AB6CE1FFAD274.description: Operations: Students will demonstrate the meaning of addition and subtraction of whole numbers and fractions and compute accurately.

83DD97220DB540319E71C7344C7C0FED.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way and record each decomposition with an equation and a visual representation.

95604E40914D4B7A8DEB24839F87515A.description: Compare and order fractions having unlike numerators and unlike denominators using visual representations (number line), comparison symbols and verbal reasoning (e.g., using benchmarks or common numerators or common denominators).

F10BC91D81F14C9BB5B1199434B87232.description: Explain how to change a mixed number to a fraction and how to change a fraction to a mixed number.

C73B091A058B4647807EE3FABFFA0519.description: Generate and explain equivalent fractions by multiplying by an equivalent fraction of 1.

AD56D585DCDA4CE7A54B9D117B3D3CC5.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators of 10 or 100.

93E19FBF4CA1434D8B093EBB1DC1A34E.description: Round a multi-digit whole number to any given place.

0506F70CF39042D3A9E462CCC85F1994.description: Compare whole numbers up to one million and decimals through the hundredths place using >, <, and = symbols, and visual representations.

389449CBD76442229FEFD9568F16BE0E.description: Determine factors of any whole number up to 100.

D606DEFED3B4488695EB26831CA5D747.description: Determine whether a given whole number up to 100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number.

1BF05AF110BF45E5ADA72F1CAFEF461B.description: Classify a number up to 100 as prime or composite.

E91695F66579442EBC829655A12F37AC.description: Recognize a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 what it represents in the place to its left.

7EA6A63D917147C29FCCCF47786EDDDC.description: Read, write, and demonstrate multiple equivalent representations for whole numbers up to one million and decimals to the hundredths, using objects, visual representations, standard form, word form, and expanded notation.

ACCDBA966DF54433B973FE5113ABC60B.description: Numeric Relationships: Students will demonstrate, represent, and show relationships among fractions and decimals within the base-ten number system.

8259EE55C0644799A3E63DACBC8DEEC1.description: Number: Students will communicate number sense concepts using multiple representations to reason, solve problems, and make connections within mathematics and across disciplines.

document.title: Nebraska K-12 Fine Arts Standards: Dance

B9B17258BE214B16B41EE4F69D802318.description: Identify various dance-related professions and how they impact the field of dance.
comments: Brainstorm and research a dance-related profession.

5149979696A64A1BB054E547D3AD15C9.description: Apply health and nutrition to enhance dance ability (e.g., set goals for healthy behaviors that may enhance dance experiences).
comments: Investigate bodywork practices, (e.g., yoga) that may remain lifelong pursuits.

8DA2369DACE8492593B5B24BFF8B8067.description: Demonstrate how other arts disciplines are integrated into dance creation and performance (e.g., understand the principles underlying collaboration by learning or creating dances in cooperation with students working in other disciplines, or by using elements and skills from other disciplines).
comments: Music: joint project with a student composer. Visual Arts: relationship between space, objects, viewer in art installations. Theatre: sing and act while dancing. Media Arts: create a music video.
Explore the influences of various global dances by researching historical, social, and cultural contexts.
EC86DABD054540348B910951DBA9A3BD.description: Use dance to apply concepts in world history and relate them to significant events, ideas, and traditions from a global context (e.g., research the role dance played globally and throughout time).

2E386844EB2541D09CD2A8639C6770C5.description: Students will apply cultural, interdisciplinary, and historical connections with dance.

B044DFA9F3964DC38C447CF016983D5A.description: Analyze the use of dance elements and choreographic forms and structures in a variety of significant, current dance works for the 21st century (e.g., implement analytical skills to examine current companies and/or choreographers).
comments: Research a contemporary, emerging choreographer and write a report. Explore a current dance company and assess requirements for admission.

115A7CBFEA66469CA714325A4C618497.description: Use accurate dance terminology to describe how elements of movement and choreographic structures are used to communicate ideas in dance (e.g., use written and verbal expression to analyze dance in response to dance observation, creation, and performance).
comments: Write a review and compare it to a professional review. View an episode of "So You Think You Can Dance" or "Dancing With the Stars." Write and compare student and judge critiques.

2D3B7DC3D9FA4129914C89090BCD0F08.description: Students will apply critical thinking skills to analyze and evaluate dance.

C0C9B814D7134C3B97D96F77916A5288.description: Understand how self-assessment, teacher, and peer feedback can be used to refine dance performance (e.g., maintain a dance portfolio: journal, research, ideas, drawings, print-media clippings, resources, and performance notes. Recognize dance may look different to an audience vs. the way it feels to a performer).
comments: Interview an audience member and a dancer to get varying views. Apply constructive criticism from feedback to future rehearsals and performances.

6A51F8EB4D2540EC801FE62095FB0C27.description: Understand the impact of performance values of clarity, concentration, focus, and projection on dance performance (e.g., understand the concepts of solo, duet, group dance, and the impact of each).
comments: Create a solo, duet or group performance reflecting a distinct personal statement. Students will conduct peer assessment.
Be respectful of the space, student, instructor and self. Ask students to list points of etiquette regarding individual genres.
2DAD4C4CFBAC4A90BD1D84511CE926A9.description: Apply appropriate behaviors and etiquette to observe, create, and perform dance (e.g., demonstrate safe practices for each genre, apply dance experience and knowledge, exhibit dance awareness).

9AEC15C0368649EE92AE814C3D96C405.description: Students will understand how to apply performance values kinesthetic awareness, concentration, focus, and etiquette to enhance dance performance.

F4388132AF7745F69EEF1D6CC7B87CAF.description: Recognize differences and execute technical skills from a variety of dance styles (e.g., study techniques such as ballet, modern, "release technique", West African, Afro-Haitian, jazz, hip-hop, rhythm tap, Broadway tap, flamenco, Broadway theater dance, latin, ballroom).
comments: After completion of multiple units find similarities in technique. Attend an outside workshop and discuss differing dance styles.

063FD6C91F8347ACBC3592F8C190F9F9.description: Apply time, space, weight, and flow to perform dance (e.g., use expressive musical phrasing and dynamic control).

5B22DE7510AE482B825C89C56B861E03.description: Use a variety of body movements with flexibility, endurance, strength, and proper alignment to develop form and execute dance technique (e.g., execute extended sequences in a variety of dance forms with a high rate of accuracy).

8AB6134A5E3447078E4C1FB15B1FE204.description: Students will apply movement skills in dance.

7705517E197D436E84E7EB41721ADE08.description: Manipulate movement ideas, choose from a variety of solutions to movement problems, and work with others to create choreography (e.g., create a group work for peers).
comments: Works may be based on an abstract concept such as time, or a concrete subject such as a personal experience.

FB61BDF1BE23440A834B6C64179824FD.description: Understand and apply the role of improvisation to create choreography with others (e.g., create cohesive transitions between the phrases).
comments: Use improvisation to create transitions. Use communication and collaboration skills to solidify choreography.

9DF0763E4C5A47D191B00A098A7B1BF4.description: Create a dance sequence that uses a variety of dance elements to implement simple choreographic structures and principles to fulfill choreographic intent (e.g., select phrases for expansion into dance sequences).
comments: Edit movement phrases by changing rhythm, tempo, dynamics, use of space.

BFD7DF44585F47A89DE64DA04221BA68.description: Generate movement and create dance phrases to communicate ideas, images, feelings, and experiences based on inspiration from a variety of sources (e.g., create a dance phrase based on a favorite song, poem, art piece).
comments: ABA form, repetition, inversion, retrograde.

963C9D8279014D7AA30B7DE84C139E33.description: Students will employ dance elements and choreographic principles, structures, and processes to create dances that communicate ideas, images, feelings, and experiences.

A236371DC5424FFB952A26CFC643623F.description: Students will develop knowledge and skills to create, perform, respond to, and connect artistic ideas and expressions through dance and movement.

document.title: Nebraska English Language Arts Standards

884D498D281B43F886CE122666CB949F.description: Use appropriate digital tools (e.g., social media, online collaborative tools, apps) to communicate with others for conveying information, gathering opinions, and solving problems.

13A4F647825E47568787DBB933C60CA0.description: Practice safe and ethical behaviors when communicating and interacting with others digitally (e.g., safe information to share, appropriate language use, utilize appropriate sites and materials, respect diverse perspectives).

55265BE08AE64E0EA17F6D8868AB6CDC.description: Digital Citizenship: Students will practice the norms of appropriate and responsible technology use.

B2E66C83A65B4CF6B92C96AED5489B39.description: Use or decipher multiple formats of print and digital text (e.g., cursive, manuscript, font, graphics, symbols).

D84A64CA5A5345BA861F7DDF8F85723B.description: With guidance, demonstrate ethical use of information and copyright guidelines by appropriately quoting or paraphrasing from a text and citing the source using available resources (e.g., online citation tools).

6357F40AF30B47D5A89833ED05ABEB7B.description: Locate, organize, and evaluate information from print and digital resources to generate and answer questions and create new understandings.

567CEA290BE34DE1BA2B1F88B50EBA49.description: Information Fluency: Students will evaluate, create, and communicate information in a variety of media and formats (textual, visual, and digital).

9770888398834B61869CCCECEB20F8C8.description: Multiple Literacies: Students will apply information fluency and practice digital citizenship.

8C38B1859EA84D9C898DCAE7EB65C547.description: Collaboratively converse with peers and adults on grade-appropriate topics and texts, building on others' ideas to clearly express one's own views while respecting diverse perspectives.

C30A6A4397D047198288E68812667369.description: Listen, ask clarifying questions, summarize, and respond to information being communicated and consider its contribution to a topic, text, or issue under study.

BF319135D3BE446B8992FF8884653B0C.description: Apply conversation strategies to recognize and consider new information presented by others in relationship to one's own ideas.

296BA2D426B347599E286D5E8AB59260.description: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., stereotypes, multiple meanings of words) in conversation.

D0FADAA225C74A3185469AFD71DF1B70.description: Demonstrate appropriate social etiquette and apply social cues when communicating.

292A7F0A7CAB4993A22BEFB55005E5E7.description: Reciprocal Communication: Students will develop, apply, and adapt reciprocal communication skills.

BB005815026B44218F405FE59FEE3BF7.description: Complete a task following multi-step directions.

8612B9C99953449B95187A2260B7442C.description: Identify the purpose and credibility of information being presented in diverse media and formats.

EA9A4AFB73144F388AC3665256E5D4E5.description: Demonstrate active and attentive listening skills (e.g., eye contact, nonverbal cues, recalling, questioning) for multiple situations and modalities.

47820F4B6D4C4906A2AD70C6BBE4A3DE.description: Listening: Students will develop and demonstrate active listening skills across a variety of situations.

94D0182CFBE34100A08583D8A62893B7.description: Ask pertinent questions to acquire or confirm information.

223B94D4DD5B478281B055AD483FEDD4.description: Convey a perspective with clear reasoning and support.

7F6AA86C3160442DBDEB638D0A6693C5.description: Utilize appropriate visual and/or digital tools to enhance verbal communication and add interest.

88DCD09F85274434BDFDBF57747B8460.description: Demonstrate appropriate speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, clear pronunciation) for a variety of purposes and situations, including interpreting text.

607AAC69456E4F52A8A6FD65CEE78DCD.description: Communicate ideas and information in a clear and concise manner suited to the purpose, setting, and audience (formal voice or informal voice), using appropriate word choice, grammar, and sentence structure.

39E5CBE76A604A6BB96CF6A9C8CBCE77.description: Speaking: Students will develop, apply, and refine speaking skills and strategies to communicate key ideas in a variety of situations.

70AA5B73D3074397BF8EAA7377C7FFDC.description: Speaking and Listening: Students will develop and apply speaking and listening skills and strategies to communicate for a variety of purposes.

ACCB97506FC34EC3BE1FC96C52294B0F.description: Compare various mentor texts and/or exemplars to create a similar piece.

500F74C05CD14F698587DFF095FC2C14.description: Use precise word choice and domain-specific vocabulary to write in a variety of modes.

E2DEC25F127F4439ACFD9DF4AFADC146.description: Conduct and publish research to answer questions or solve problems using multiple resources to support theses.

4E67AFBCB8FC46429C981D732FA05B28.description: Provide evidence from literary or informational text to support ideas or opinions.

58CB172CAD1C47CF92399B90F094EDA0.description: Communicate information and ideas effectively in analytic, descriptive, informative, narrative, poetic, persuasive, and reflective modes to multiple audiences using a variety of media and formats.

05A8E52B99D8426EA1CDFB8BA3C1F6AA.description: Writing Modes: Student will write in multiple modes for a variety of purposes and audiences across disciplines.

88FEC7AB6DE44CB181D441B14EE8BDF6.description: Publish a legible document in manuscript, cursive, or digital format, and apply formatting techniques (e.g., indenting paragraphs, title).

6A490A0C54764415A9269DB54425B6DA.description: Display academic honesty and integrity by avoiding plagiarism and/or overreliance on any one source and by following a standard format for citation.

9CC713ADF31B49978BE29613735555F8.description: Proofread and edit writing recursively for format and conventions of standard English (e.g., spelling, capitalization, grammar, punctuation, syntax, semantics).

53C6B3094DF741EFAC3BCF1D0C8D35FD.description: Adjust writing processes to persevere in short and long-term writing tasks of increasing length and complexity.

B4B34CF30A954699B56C2B6CFFCBEC90.description: Provide oral and/or written descriptive feedback to other writers.

2E7A72D15D8F4DC384C8AC2CF4FF58F2.description: Revise to improve and clarify writing through self-monitoring strategies and feedback from others.

E1C99EBAF1E94006BCFFB618A958AE22.description: Compose paragraphs with grammatically correct sentences of varying length, complexity, and type.

604A81B3059044F8ABE3BC83B777BDD7.description: Gather and use relevant information and evidence from one or more authoritative print and/or digital sources to support claims or theses.

3CC2C8148763453C95D5C5481FB011C4.description: Generate a draft that develops a clear topic suited to the purpose and intended audience and organizational pattern, including a clear introduction, body, and conclusion with appropriate transitions.

32DAD29376DD4A5DBA1FAE9F98161228.description: Use prewriting activities and inquiry tools to generate ideas and organize information.

6F3646705305406090537597544888A4.description: Writing Process: Students will apply the writing process to plan, draft, revise, edit, and publish writing using correct spelling, grammar, punctuation, and other conventions of standard English appropriate for grade-level.

5D4C95BEE41246C3AF9A4F47A98A2F49.description: Writing: Students will learn and apply writing skills and strategies to communicate.

FDCE7DC5020C4A4D9EB5476589F8E024.description: Make connections between the text of a story, drama, or poem and a visual or oral presentation of the text.

9629C9A2B4B6498EB3839D2B022B609F.description: Demonstrate an understanding of text via multiple mediums (e.g., writing, artistic representation, video, other media).

65FAA0BEF51B4BC29CF848B4A8BBFD50.description: Make and confirm/modify predictions and inferences before, during, and after reading literary, informational, digital text, and/or media.

335D2CFCE65D42CD95AF8CB8D0D1C85C.description: Self-monitor comprehension by recognizing when meaning is disrupted and apply strategies to clarify, confirm, or correct.

1CB23DAE9F29477092DAA45BCEBD2802.description: Build background knowledge and activate prior knowledge to identify text-to-self, text-to-text, and text-to-world connections before, during, and after reading.

8D4B2AF04AB840DBA140B33253B2385E.description: Select text and explain the purpose (e.g., answer a question, solve problems, enjoy, form an opinion, understand a specific viewpoint, predict outcomes, discover models for own writing, accomplish a task).

FE7F0B8A01E44F5F81899F5F36575043.description: Identify and apply knowledge of organizational patterns to comprehend informational text (e.g., sequence, description, cause and effect, compare/contrast).

59905172CE914DA7AB25E5C4A06AA2BD.description: Construct and/or answer literal and inferential questions and support answers with specific evidence from the text or additional sources.

EBD16083ADE248AE8AA468B3CF20181B.description: Compare and contrast similar themes, topics, and/or patterns of events in literary and informational texts to develop a multicultural perspective.

8113C74F64584FFAA1EE0255C2A7CF03.description: Compare and contrast the characteristics that distinguish a variety of literary and informational texts.

96A9AEEF1978426C8B3D145367E92CA8.description: Use text features to locate information and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of print and digital text.

1FCF89F8CB1B49A28DF74EC273F27F37.description: Determine main ideas and supporting details from informational text and/or media.

7195538EE4C647E9AE8286C6E10C406C.description: Summarize a literary text and/or media, using key details to identify the theme.

DC83957D20FE4BA7B83F9ECD54AEDACD.description: Identify and explain why authors use literary devices (e.g., simile, alliteration, onomatopoeia, imagery, rhythm, personification, hyperbole, idioms).

7B1091C0B9864BB2804427EEEFD1DEBA.description: Identify and describe elements of literary text (e.g., characters, setting, plot, point of view).

FC4A9778FBFB4F7C915B4904847F9899.description: Identify author's purpose(s) (e.g., explain, entertain, inform, persuade) to support text comprehension.

619779B4144745C8B2BAE9A5461AD30F.description: Comprehension: Students will construct meaning by using prior knowledge and text information while reading grade-level literary and informational text.

51D772B1ABF94B89850A5E02064D4C52.description: Locate words and determine meaning using reference materials.

91EA73102D414EE386ACCA0005AF31E7.description: Identify semantic relationships (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs, homophones, multiple-meaning words) to determine the meaning of words, aid in comprehension, and improve writing.

B2691C1A26D042C4B343BEDAE178A0B7.description: Acquire new academic and content-specific grade-level vocabulary, relate to prior knowledge, and apply in new situations.

0F9F33D2090946ECBFC6D40AAE953CAC.description: Apply context clues (e.g., word, phrase, and sentence clues) and text features to help infer meaning of unknown words.

4945D37528E045DD8BFAE97ED5B821EF.description: Determine meaning of words through the knowledge of word structure elements, known words, and word patterns (e.g., contractions, plurals, possessives, parts of speech, syllables, affixes, base and root words, abbreviations).

595709C2CACF4409AD4DF784C7087268.description: Vocabulary: Students will build and use conversational, academic, and content-specific grade-level vocabulary.

D78B4EE79E574F0A9C6ADCDAE934E920.description: Use context to adjust pace and prosody based on purpose, text complexity, form, and style.

EADB6AFC2149415C9317DFF380E21DD2.description: Listen to and read text of increasing length and/or complexity to increase reader stamina.

54CA855DB6B6432C8EFF0EAB8D7AB274.description: Fluency: Students will develop accuracy, phrasing, and expression while reading a variety of grade-level print/digital text to support comprehension.

5DEC26F2113B49BE8BBA78D1A0C392A4.description: Recognize and read grade-level (phonetic and non-phonetic) words in text.

3D33EF6F2BAE48B38BAB60616C17BEA5.description: Use word structure to read text (e.g., prefixes/suffixes contractions, syllabication, derivation).

9B8DB2E174E04ADCB45FEE9F6DFA0995.description: Know and apply advanced sound/spelling patterns (e.g., Anglo-Saxon common roots and affixes, special vowel spellings [ough, ion], multi-syllable words) when reading, writing, and spelling grade-level text.

420905A651BE4957A51D27AE3D8D08B4.description: Word Analysis: Students will use phonetic analysis to read and write grade-level text.

5CA6FB14A4294789891139D448888757.description: Phonological Awareness: Students will demonstrate phonological awareness through oral activities.
comments: Mastered in Grade 1 and blended with other skills at this grade level.

DD313D02F99D4A44B941A31B38C8BCC4.description: Concepts of Print: Students will demonstrate knowledge of the concepts of print.
comments: Mastered in Grade 1 and blended with other skills at this grade level.

ECC89889CCDA40BBA9F6B87C7643AE5D.description: Reading: Students will learn and apply reading skills and strategies to comprehend text.

document.title: Nebraska K-12 Fine Arts Standards: Media Arts

69148B1E4B504553B4D3E124815DD0E9.description: Identify the importance of media arts as a learning tool.

CBFB1CA0026E4E7BA239EB5AA44194E0.description: Explore use of media arts as a collaborative art form to communicate information, experiences, or ideas to others.

9B5B4FADF9E443C2BFF0DF45658AE864.description: Share and discuss the characteristics of digital citizenship (glossary) (e.g., copyright, plagiarism).

1EB044D2E50141EDB48854838A018624.description: Investigate media arts connections to school, community, and everyday life (e.g., websites, advertising).

8B94FBCF9BA846E498A2FCC252DBDC8B.description: Students will explore personal and cultural connections through media arts.

28B394BC372E4E79AA1577D29496E1B4.description: Discuss how media arts experiences can shift individual understanding.

EB876CFAF5D04765B46601BD010C8CE6.description: Identify different elements that make up media arts and how they make us feel (e.g., background music, imaging, timing).

3BAC762266144C0490887178A130B016.description: Students will explore the concept of interpretation through media arts.

F26121D6DAB940BA84F9F19974BC3EAB.description: Share or distribute media arts in a safe and appropriate venue (e.g., school website, student information system).

E22938FF57A6462584CAC394590916EC.description: Understand self and others as an audience with guided reflection. (e.g., who, what, when, where, why).

573ABBA7272641B7B61D00A301C541A7.description: Practice manipulating media and context for personal expression in media arts productions.

8BAB271F9F77474BB61CFDF1C4C38EEA.description: Introduce cooperation, negotiation, and communication in creating media arts (e.g., collaborative posters).

B8C590C0C6674509B4C7A00EDA09A73A.description: Students will explore ways to communicate an idea/message in media arts.

A7AC2EFAD7AF437EB56C24D8E50428BF.description: Introduce understanding of, and respect for, the accepted procedures regarding the responsible care of media arts equipment and materials.

AC30887454564AB384FDFD50A112FFC5.description: Explore various editing tools on existing media to create media arts (e.g., capture, copy, paste).

74F3C8DCADE547E18533426BCB751531.description: Determine the steps, vocabulary, and the resources necessary to create media arts.

D74363EC7F5647FF8A089DB492F0D703.description: Share imaginative ways that media arts can be used to communicate a narrative, experience, or idea (e.g., movie, podcast, digital art).

024200C5FAC947F99566F2AD79E455BD.description: Students will explore creative processes and techniques in media arts.

BDBAB23A03AF4B1084424D2C3D22902D.description: Students will develop knowledge and skills of current and emerging processes, techniques, and applications used in the creation of media arts as a means of expressing human experience.

document.title: Nebraska K-12 Fine Arts Standards: Theatre

EA6A2D91F3B84BD29B8693C523346766.description: Respect intellectual property rights and identify entities vital to creation of, and advocacy for, theatre (e.g., respecting author intent, crediting authors, royalties, publishing companies, community theatres).

E899E9216FD14D959B0D1F6B529E6281.description: Connect and draw conclusions about how various jobs in theatre contribute to the whole theatrical experience.

35E7CB4F97F8469893CE59316F100B21.description: Analyze and evaluate cultural impact of theatre on society (e.g., A Raisin in the Sun, West Side Story).

4EDDACAEB12741F595B972C0FAD90F52.description: Examine the convergence of themes, ethics, aesthetics, and traditions in a theatrical work.

DA3D3BC459904A33ABDB67EF5EB8B63E.description: Explain the differences between historical event and dramatization of the event (e.g., The Diary of Anne Frank vs. the play The Diary of Anne Frank, Salem Witch Trial records vs. The Crucible, letters of Abigail and John Adams vs. the musical 1776).

D459A970CCE6450783C69A41B2EB9745.description: Analyze the cultural and historical significance of theatrical forms as they have evolved over time, including contemporary theatre and pop culture (e.g., Romeo and Juliet influenced West Side Story).

54F91F03954D468F975D6F243EB87330.description: Students will analyze and evaluate connections between theatre and society.

C62AA80B75B54AB0AB4543C84E04DA31.description: Justify a personal reaction to a performance or recording of a live performance.

91CCCC211C9948308CB50610FBAAF4D3.description: Differentiate among theatrical works as dramatic, comedic, musical theatre, or tragic genres.

38EBAC5605154A44888071EB0BF68627.description: Evaluate how choices of the actor(s) impact audience understanding of a performance (e.g., Hamlet (Mel Gibson, Kenneth Branagh), multiple versions of Romeo & Juliet).

90E9FC6AFD5744388A3482E2D2AD9021.description: Analyze and critique in part, or in its entirety, a live performance or recording of a live performance.

E338968CCEDB4E6C9B229DFE99162837.description: Evaluate how audience conduct affects a theatrical performance.

60349C73CDAB4E65B8B572204D0920E7.description: Students will analyze and evaluate audience/performance relationship.

EE47BB3436BE478292AED4ACFA3133E1.description: Demonstrate understanding/respect for accepted procedures regarding responsible use/care of theatrical equipment/material (e.g., show awareness of fire codes regarding lights, curtains, paint storage, seating, scene shops; knowledge of rigging standards, safety regulations for use of power tools and other equipment).

1A7C604111D940FFB6FA0E15587933F9.description: Evaluate one's own effectiveness in a production/scene (e.g., taking director feedback and modifying performance).

86A672987DA64EDD9E7EC4ACDA3EA788.description: Design and craft a performance space making effective use of available light, sound, and color.

2B2CD77D89834ECE8DD189132C59BBA0.description: Expand and develop character based on teacher/director comments.

69249DDC0C8741CFBA9C02BC74737430.description: Polish and perform a monologue (glossary) based on the character developed in previous strand ("create character" FA 12.5.1.f).

43958B4048BD47A4B4877C7E5A41AE1E.description: Rehearse, refine, and perform a scripted play incorporating a designed environment and audience arrangement.

FF069D7FCD3A431A9694B10145B335E6.description: Communicate character, relationship, and objective through the use of blocking and facial expression (e.g., duet scene from Romeo & Juliet, Mama and Walter from Raisin in the Sun, Joe Mondragon and Sheriff from The Milagro Beanfield War).

240F75EA2358481FB1D1B331DE7EBD2F.description: Communicate character through the use of rate, articulation, enunciation, projection, inflection, blocking in a monologue or scene.

744C5BEFD7A845D3A2680C08B03E8E5C.description: Students will perform ideas and events through movement, speech, and staging for an intended audience.

897DA46F25B545CABF8A5C3CD2882414.description: Plan and rehearse an invented, historical or fictional character using posture, movement, facial expression, gestures, vocal choice, costume, make-up, hair, props, and space (e.g., living history monologue, Miracle Worker, Of Mice and Men, Pony Boy from The Outsiders)

41726E409E5B491BB37FD9F88857C5F8.description: Adapt a section or scene for performance from a novel or short story using dialogue and/or narration (e.g., trial scene from To Kill A Mockingbird, "The Interview" from The Scarlet Letter, Speak, "The Lottery").

11B9F0451D8B477A9A0784B8D8E53A80.description: Analyze themes within theatrical works and their social relevance to audiences (e.g., McCarthyism in Arthur Miller's The Crucible).

26B46285BF544F169772C3B640FBD73D.description: Develop and refine, through improvisation, a short scene using linear plot structure.

0DF1BC7D89314F038D77D8E2747C6344.description: Create a storyboard of an event using non-linear plot structure.

79494A34B898433B996A6C5E5F1F5117.description: Design, develop, and use an environment with available materials appropriate to a scripted or improvised performance (e.g., plan and create a bus stop or a store front).

44C3F8C468234A959499DED7034D3420.description: Students will dramatize ideas and events using linear and non-linear plot structures.

EEA17451B06043328FD2F8158F0C6F15.description: Students will develop knowledge and skills applying the creative and collaborative process within theatre by crafting, performing, and responding to expressions of the human experience.

document.title: Nebraska K-12 Fine Arts Standards: Visual Arts

033AE128D99A49D4A265D26E276351DF.description: Explain how images and objects are used to convey a story, familiar experience, or connection to the world.

1C2875414D3C4D3E92F87090EBDACC62.description: Compare and contrast the purpose and function of different art forms. (e.g., artifacts vs. fine art).

AA9F95813ED940FC97DBF0FD09C6B1C1.description: Investigate and classify works of art from a variety of contemporary, historical, and cultural contexts.

772E197E6DBD44428E751F46D8023EED.description: Students can identify and demonstrate the role of an artist and explore art-related career opportunities.

80CD6D898BE74BA59A1D2C4633DB7F76.description: Students will examine the significance of art in contemporary, historical, and cultural context in art and life.

192253A013C4460F80D9A5E8F6512508.description: Connect – Individual perspective and identity through the study of art

53E1A67AE2A44C3A9CD8D1EC25E14874.description: Explore how the meaning of art can be affected by the presentation mode or venue (e.g., reproduction, digital, social media, or original museum/gallery experience).

A53E15A3A3E1450ABA1E4CDCCC19EFE8.description: Analyze, individually and collaboratively, the selection of art collections, displays, and presentations.

9968A680E4454DB2824E7A29DF7127E5.description: Analyze and present reflections of personal growth in an artist statement.

F4C791662E7C4C98BB69C3A8B32591AD.description: Students will understand and apply their knowledge of a variety of presentation and communication techniques.

FE7A8476CB00417180A8C093C64B35B8.description: Present – Art to communicate ideas, process, and product.

F99A485ED91A442FA7F3FE0A26BE3737.description: Explain why a work of art can evoke different interpretations and how artwork is interpreted and evaluated by the way it is displayed or presented.

88C7DE8F4B014D77B722E707F1FA6C07.description: Compare and contrast various interpretations of themes, styles, and mood.

BD42D98B29544ACBB3CD5DCD0C6D8743.description: Compare and contrast works of art using elements and principles (e.g., themes, styles, cultures).

B0CE47F4908849D79A46B5D85FA88731.description: Identify and describe themes and styles in works of art.

E0F34E94B4824C19833129A472D1A6B7.description: Students will use the critical process to compare and contrast multiple works of art, learning about themselves in the world.

7D83F74DEE1B443EB6A8F56CFBCBED81.description: Respond – to understand and appreciate ideas

079BA8DC0FCB4FDAB484AB9B5CF68DEE.description: Demonstrate respect for accepted procedures regarding responsible care of equipment and materials.

4FF0EAB1F3754A5B8590B2314DBB4B2A.description: Investigate and demonstrate the relationship between technique, skill, and craftsmanship.

9D25EFBB1A934A0EADC6E3B836099D25.description: Investigate and apply relationships between elements of art and principles of design to brainstorm visual possibilities (e.g., consider a variety of images and determine how line and value create emphasis in art).

0F6F1A33615547818AB300D22B2E6ADD.description: Engage in the sensory experience and relate it to making expressive artwork.

35CE2128C9094D68809831E59CB81DE1.description: Recognize personal voice and make stylistic choices to reflect personal identity.

F9B71D44FF734A0697B5946F7AB8213E.description: Investigate ideas and materials to demonstrate planning and refining.

A53676BC1BC7440B9EBF131101BE4FC2.description: Students will use the creative process to investigate and communicate personal voice in artwork.

216A2EF62CD146FDB2B03ED853F29AA2.description: Students will develop and apply ideas, knowledge, and skills to create, respond to, present, and connect art with the human experience. (curricular bands have been re-ordered: create, respond, present, connect)

document.title: Nebraska English Language Arts Standards

E7576F0D05A245019A45846944A6710B.description: Use appropriate digital tools (e.g., social media, online collaborative tools, apps) to communicate with others for conveying information, gathering opinions, and solving problems.

EC60B10F04D046C589F8418536761825.description: With guidance, demonstrate ethical use of information and copyright guidelines by appropriately quoting or paraphrasing from a text and citing the source using available resources (e.g., online citation tools).

ACF869E6853B4D6EA665355ABF364361.description: With guidance, use provided print and digital resources to gather information, answer questions, and demonstrate understanding of valid information (e.g., fiction vs. nonfiction, real vs. not real).

2AD9B09ADED845059610851BB71A4A82.description: Information Fluency: Students will evaluate, create, and communicate information in a variety of media and formats (textual, visual, and digital).

E461D83C2DA3411986C971F08996DAF7.description: Collaboratively converse with peers and adults on grade-appropriate topics and texts, building on others' ideas to clearly express one's own views while respecting diverse perspectives.

12C2F24A30454A54AB1745B6FBC87F44.description: Listen, ask clarifying questions, and respond to information being communicated about a topic, text, or issue under study.

1B455D9F66D643CC895DC4B8924354F3.description: Apply conversation strategies to recognize new information presented by others in relationship to one's own ideas.

58E918CBC74247CEA57F02EEFA9BF521.description: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., helpful/hurtful words) in conversation.

394FFFD7F3904E6AAE630CF2F9C57325.description: Practice appropriate classroom etiquette and recognize social cues when communicating.

BBFB0364C8C2468BBA27B8892E16BDF8.description: Reciprocal Communication: Students will develop, apply, and adapt reciprocal communication skills.

9AAEA7A104B74C66A7790BFC798A6D6C.description: Complete a task following one/two-step directions.

C3BDCDDD39D84A9EABB3E3E66D0640E4.description: With adult guidance, discuss the purpose and credibility of information being presented in diverse media and formats.

77A615700F8A4065BC65B0A144A18784.description: Develop active and attentive listening skills (e.g., eye contact, nonverbal cues, recalling) for multiple situations and modalities.

88B31FCD7B354919B57090DF7804B5B4.description: Listening: Students will develop and demonstrate active listening skills across a variety of situations.

B606B274D5F04EB2B792D12D04F0162A.description: Ask pertinent questions to acquire or confirm information.

197FA40C0042478283A42F3908E92DCF.description: Convey a personal perspective with clear reasons.

C05508291B4E4816B745FBA3F6107237.description: Utilize appropriate visual and/or digital tools to support verbal communication.

7E591C6B1CF948789A501F037E420D73.description: Demonstrate appropriate speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, clear pronunciation) for a variety of purposes and situations.

9CC969EE787140E0BA6029AEB9B1716B.description: Communicate ideas clearly to others within structured classroom activities and routines using appropriate word choice, proper grammar, and complete sentences.

CC4C04CFD5DD4D63B01064D1A3941AAE.description: Speaking: Students will develop, apply and refine speaking skills and strategies to communicate key ideas in a variety of situations.

0229EFB8B93749859D1EF33F84A08B70.description: Speaking and Listening: Students will develop and apply speaking and listening skills and strategies to communicate for a variety of purposes.

54E2743288D64887A9067A6F0324DDEC.description: With adult guidance, compare mentor texts and examples to create similar pieces.

DF4A8B56997A4700B392A48263AC7C5E.description: Use precise word choice and domain-specific vocabulary to write in a variety of modes.

CC1C243B057C40ACB63779056B22E23B.description: With adult guidance, conduct and publish research to answer questions or solve problems.

7715DA03042A4B4B97D7457B1D5F7AF3.description: With adult guidance, provide evidence from literary or informational text to support ideas or opinions.

A7C41B84570A4A50BB9CBEB61E36EB00.description: Communicate information and ideas effectively in analytic, descriptive, informative, narrative, poetic, persuasive, and reflective modes to multiple audiences using a variety of media and formats.

3D0A818209B24797B22756699817821C.description: Writing Modes: Student will write in multiple modes for a variety of purposes and audiences across disciplines.

844E1C72165944AF9C4979716655C5E4.description: With adult guidance, publish a legible document with appropriate spaces between letters, words, and sentences in a variety of formats.

1C33E291DB0F4A50BAAF522416CDEEC6.description: Use own words to relate information.

ADB196B6BAB84ACCAFBD1F0B9FE167D2.description: With adult guidance, proofread and edit writing recursively for format and conventions of standard English (e.g., spelling, capitalization, grammar, punctuation).

29E8B9A65CA64EA095018C68E06C3415.description: With adult guidance, persevere in writing tasks.

ED7D08ABC8134A8EBB65B27DFA94AC9F.description: Provide oral descriptive feedback to other writers.

12492613A4084137B67EF1B1241F5623.description: With adult guidance, revise to improve and clarify writing through self-monitoring strategies and feedback from others.

81E4876BBE3142F7A32D55D33611436A.description: With adult guidance, use relevant information and evidence to support ideas.

271512670C224220AFB3CE65514360DE.description: Generate representations of ideas (e.g., pictures, labels, letter strings, words, simple sentences) and organize ideas relevant to a topic.

4BFC32AE64EE4270BDC82AAA8C1CEE45.description: Use prewriting activities and inquiry tools to generate ideas.

520646F60BD945CA84D407F71B9C253E.description: Writing Process: Students will apply the writing process to plan, draft, revise, edit, and publish writing using correct spelling, grammar, punctuation, and other conventions of standard English appropriate for grade-level.

770FBE42A578498F913670A5D7066047.description: Writing: Students will learn and apply writing skills and strategies to communicate.

4B89998C9B804942B31194DD6FE7E7FB.description: Make connections between a print text and an audio, video, or live version of the text.

DA685EC8E7FE4FEB9FD429566C60321E.description: Respond to text (e.g., verbally, in writing, or artistically).

3BF131DC54FD48E0831997AFB412189C.description: Make predictions about a text using prior knowledge, pictures, illustrations, and titles.

3B56DD941874457DAE45B2BD35CB595D.description: With adult guidance, monitor comprehension by recognizing when meaning is disrupted.

84E79E6CF35E48E49994B059511675A7.description: Build background knowledge and activate prior knowledge to identify text-to-self, text-to-text, and text-to-world connections.

5ED28B1DD42041E3BE74C8716BBEC114.description: Identify different purposes for reading (e.g., inform, enjoy).

C8127D2CE1534B818C3C37F8314F45B8.description: Identify the characteristics of organizational patterns found in informational text (e.g., sequence, compare/contrast).

9B4D0EA6AC74436F9F6D5EADC69208AB.description: Construct and/or answer clarifying questions (who, what, when, where, why, how) and support answers with evidence from the text or additional sources.

67D03A27314547B3AEA5300DDA53DC54.description: Make connections between own life and/or other cultures in literary and informational text.

11227842936249F5BE24152FC85FC891.description: Identify the basic characteristics of literary and informational text.

233905DD86094C5B9F08AE2214611A55.description: Identify text features in print and digital informational text.

0448A9AA9ED0453587686BC668B80963.description: With adult guidance, retell main ideas from informational text and/or media.

A0DEEA18FEA84AAE96C66C98A7C6146A.description: With adult guidance, retell major events and key details from a literary text and/or media.

7990694F13374C78AA1369AF31FE2EA0.description: With adult guidance, identify an author's use of literary devices (e.g., rhyme, rhythm, repetition, alliteration).

5C7118E634DE4A77AB665C2159EC113D.description: Identify elements of literary text (e.g., characters, setting, events).

D6E899198FB24557BD341EADF8AAB4CC.description: With adult guidance, identify author's purpose (e.g., explain, entertain, inform).

E86D9C6450CD42238C4EA7835BAAC08D.description: Comprehension: Students will construct meaning by using prior knowledge while reading emergent literary and informational text.

A88F0AC380D74DF998759034C760D36F.description: With adult guidance, determine word meaning using reference materials and classroom resources.

A9C32CD841844F80B18467BEEF9CFA9F.description: Identify semantic relationships (e.g., conceptual categories) to determine word relationships.

E3E7E83F990E4D749AD018280171A537.description: Acquire new academic and content-specific grade-level vocabulary, relate to prior knowledge, and apply in new situations.

D9542387F36845B281623B8052258170.description: Develop awareness of context clues (e.g., predictions, word and sentence clues) and text features that may be used to infer the meaning of unknown words.

7BE8455B7A634093A3311F52C37F0D5F.description: Examine word structure elements and word patterns to determine meaning (e.g., plural forms, simple compounds).

A3A1D98216CE485EA8E2CBED274EC86C.description: Vocabulary: Students will build and use conversational, academic, and content-specific grade-level vocabulary.

D966BBCE87D64CA1930F6FA6C0342B78.description: Use appropriate expression to reflect meaning while reading emergent-reader text.

ABE8405E1D5C44B39B33E126739878E1.description: Listen to text of increasing length and/or complexity to develop stamina.

29E1B8DDBB0241A5A0044B1A491EC16E.description: Fluency: Students will develop accuracy, phrasing, and expression during grade-level reading experiences to support comprehension.

F49685AB3AC84628848213DFDD8638DF.description: Recognize and read grade-level (phonetic and non-phonetic) words in text.

EEB7053A6CAE492BB78CE35A74D1A204.description: Identify similarities and differences in written words (e.g., word endings, onsets, rimes).

7EE3204DD9B6444596D42C963CA173FC.description: Match individual consonant and short vowel sounds to appropriate letters when reading, writing, and spelling grade-level text.

61103C1721CB4B56ABB9CFEF3FCDAFAC.description: Word Analysis: Students will acquire phonetic knowledge as they learn to read and write grade-level text.

AA488DBAA2C6430DA6A9B16E68A60858.description: Blend and segment spoken onsets and rimes to form simple words (e.g., v-an, gr-ab).

588FA571EDE6433DAC876E8B61FD6CF0.description: Identify, blend and segment syllable sounds in spoken words (e.g., cupcake, birthday).

F44E176299484C7798EEC6E1CE78086F.description: Blend and segment phonemes in spoken words (e.g., initial, medial vowel, and final sounds [phonemes]; recognize same sounds in different words).

F4E749F0D3AD456F850CD4F4A8E1328E.description: Phonological Awareness: Students will demonstrate phonological awareness through oral activities.

E1267F58D9C749C7BA047B08EECC5037.description: Demonstrate understanding that words are made up of letters and sentences are made up of words.

DED425CEAF524976B2E1CC960CD06ACF.description: Demonstrate voice to print match (e.g., student points to print while reading or as someone reads).

3BFD4A34D70D4EA791F77BFDE7FE4993.description: Explain that the purpose of print is to carry information (e.g., environmental print, nametags, street signs).

2E1D9407762E4274A44E982BD786818E.description: Demonstrate knowledge that print reads from left to right and top to bottom.

CC5EA34A141C44EEA2C371AF99F25E24.description: Identify parts of a book (e.g., cover, pages, title, author, illustrator).

2CC4B62E60FE41798D93F4DED0AFD52F.description: Identify punctuation (e.g., period, exclamation mark, question mark).

61337520FE72402F98CEE26DC28F1A8B.description: Identify variations in text (e.g., font, size, bold, italic, upper/lower case).

D6FBBEDC4057406DB2442DE681C03D34.description: Concepts of Print: Students will demonstrate knowledge of the concepts of print.

9284CF7E4D944BC7A1EAE843099E1CD6.description: Reading: Students will learn and apply reading skills and strategies to comprehend text.

document.title: Nebraska Mathematics Standards

1C3371A04A83449B8ED373748E6F9D45.description: No additional indicator(s) at this level.

54A3E6F0A6154980B57A5FF23AC459DF.description: Analysis & Applications: Students will analyze data to address the situation.

9F55DB2970574F97BDA0CBD77C28838C.description: No additional indicator(s) at this level.

4D1EF797E9B04C92B89E0864B4194331.description: Describe measurable attributes of real-world objects (e.g., length or weight).

11C57883B83547188C7C8275985046BB.description: Measurement: Students will perform and compare measurements and apply formulas.

document.title: Nebraska K-12 Fine Arts Standards: Dance

6F511FE5334A4DF6B887CFA34001CC57.description: Recognize that jobs in dance are possible.

comments: Contribute to a list of favorite foods; discuss the relationship between food, energy and exercise.

D7842FC4BD014946A1F9F37224B8B844.description: Use other arts disciplines to support ideation for dance creation and performance (e.g., understand how music, visual art, media and theatre can be combined with dance).
comments: Add music to your movement. Use artwork to inspire movement. Take turns filming each other. Tell a story through movement.

66BC8595B05E4214BA450A26C6D52755.description: Use dance to connect to social events, ideas, and traditions (e.g., list the reasons people dance, sharing personal dance experiences; family events, social gatherings, to express emotions).
comments: Create a word/picture wall using these examples.

C7FAEF8A30E44325B0B433FFE0EB3F27.description: Explore and discuss how elements of movement are used to communicate ideas in dance (e.g., encourage students to use descriptive words to explore imagery).
comments: View photos or videos of dance and discuss imagery, shapes, and ideas. Discuss student-generated free movement activities.

67577901386B4BD2BEDA05F502299C6C.description: Students will explore critical thinking skills to evaluate dance.

comments: Raise hand to give positive feedback, polite applause.

comments: Skip, hop, march, sway, swing, spin, jump.

comments: Create circles, triangles, squares, chains. Create smaller groups within the larger group

6DD551D3D70743C4A4F4538A7DB1D377.description: Identify and explain why authors use literary devices (e.g., simile, metaphor, alliteration, onomatopoeia, imagery, rhythm, personification, hyperbole, idioms, analogy, tone, mood).

D0A1D41FB66842B793E23BA036220007.description: Analyze and explain the relationships between elements of literary text (e.g., character development, setting, plot, conflict, point of view, theme).

E08A5C8C081D4DDE89D61FE622798FAD.description: Analyze text to determine author's purpose(s) and describe how author's perspective influences text.

0D10CD135EF4432DA45CA95C622D2DC7.description: Identify and use semantic relationships (e.g., multiple meanings, metaphors, similes, idioms, analogies, synonyms, antonyms) to determine the meaning of words, aid in comprehension, and improve writing.

D407DEF41194460FBA52064634708F08.description: Determine the meaning of words through structural analysis, using knowledge of Greek, Latin, and Anglo Saxon roots, prefixes, and suffixes to understand complex words, including words across content areas.

document.title: Nebraska English Language Arts Standards

1825DD63FA5048CCAD9F9F11F1D832E7.description: Use appropriate digital tools (e.g., social media, online collaborative tools, apps) to communicate with others for conveying information, gathering opinions, and solving problems.

B1497430708845678830E3D5D5FC1587.description: Listen, ask probing questions, and interpret information being communicated and consider its contribution to a topic, text, or issue under study.

7A7DCBB0B83547028B297FE0C9A02D90.description: Apply conversation strategies to recognize, consider, and explain new information presented by others in relationship to one's own ideas.

8F59664C79404576851FAF250A8EBDC8.description: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., stereotypes, connotations, subtleties of language) in conversation.

E223957CC53D4289A5A628B3AFE1B911.description: Apply appropriate social etiquette and practice social protocols when communicating.

73C118CB25024295B95701FB21E2493D.description: Reciprocal Communication: Students will develop, apply, and adapt reciprocal communication skills.

F4B4767751D24D9685E90E56D325E54F.description: Publish a legible document using a variety of media, and apply formatting techniques to enhance the readability and impact of the document (e.g., fonts, spacing, design, images, citations).

E6A07C78B6DD4ED79445D72DC5CB52B3.description: Display academic honesty and integrity by avoiding plagiarism and/or overreliance on any one source and by following a standard format for citation.

7BE78A83BDA840D9AC7A5E864D44BEE3.description: Proofread and edit writing recursively for format and conventions of standard English (e.g., spelling, capitalization, grammar, punctuation, syntax, semantics).

CF55BF7D55F148EF973C6CC26BCD11FE.description: Adjust writing processes to persevere in short and long-term writing tasks of increasing length and complexity.

0905C4DA87484DD3BA274675AE30D4C7.description: Provide oral, written, and/or digital descriptive feedback to other writers.

D15D42C2D345449993541B1EC2827D55.description: Revise to improve and clarify writing through self-monitoring strategies and feedback from others.

F8BF644FC15A4F8ABC655905FDC8F4C2.description: Compose paragraphs with grammatically correct simple, compound, and complex sentences of varying length and complexity.

FCED1A2DDE41442681C4FECAF94C74DE.description: Gather and use relevant information and evidence from multiple authoritative print and/or digital sources including primary and secondary sources to support claims or theses.

E31BD637E8A74DC4A73C8B0900EAE780.description: Generate a draft that conveys complex ideas through analysis and use of organizational patterns that are suited to the purpose and intended audience and includes a strong thesis, body, conclusion, and appropriate transitions linked to the purpose of the composition.

470A77DDE84A4BFA8D21FD416005C37E.description: Use prewriting activities and inquiry tools to recursively generate ideas, organize information, guide writing, answer questions, and synthesize information.

304927C0258F483EA3170883ED0F8194.description: Writing Process: Students will apply the writing process to plan, draft, revise, edit, and publish writing using correct spelling, grammar, punctuation, and other conventions of standard English appropriate for grade-level.

D7E164FAD9DF4B8FA2025AB050242300.description: Writing: Students will learn and apply writing skills and strategies to communicate.

7B74C009EA774A499472E1127D403467.description: Cite specific textual evidence to analyze and make inferences based on the characteristics of a variety of literary and informational texts.

document.title: Nebraska K-12 Fine Arts Standards: Dance

944D9339F1DA435EA02BFAC9EFCF4269.description: Investigate a variety of dance-related professions and the necessary training.

0AB84476F7354F9A832EBFC0879B47F6.description: Understand how dance has the ability to enhance physical and emotional health (e.g., recognize shifting moods and the ways dance can help explore and move through them).
comments: Create a dance describing an emotion.

B74CC8DEDFBA46D6BC0B049C16E5700A.description: Analyze how other arts and academic disciplines are integrated into dance creation and performance (e.g., recognize who, what, when, where, why, and how it connects to other disciplines when creating dance pieces).
comments: Discuss technical elements (e.g., costume, set, lighting) that convey the "givens" of a piece of literature.

B2A409F7704747D6A1AA8E0052DAF652.description: Use dance to understand concepts in U.S. history and relate them to significant events, ideas, and traditions from a national context (e.g., investigate what role dance played in U.S. history).
comments: Choose a style of dance, and explore the origins and people who pioneered the dance form.

E015417B8062423AA711CE9855B0A11A.description: Students will understand cultural, interdisciplinary, and historical connections with dance.

7A35CCDF6A5F44BDA79C6292E4559522.description: Recognize and discuss the use of dance elements and choreographic forms and structures in a variety of dance compositions (e.g., view live or recorded dance performance and discuss, compare, and contrast).

237C23D88DDB4459ABD4C61C465E2DB2.description: Explain and interpret how elements of movement and choreographic structures are used to communicate ideas in dance (e.g., encourage students to analyze movements in order to explore imagery and give perception).
comments: Research the connections between dance styles. Discover the uses of cultural dances in order to communicate.

C1163EDCE63D42FBBD295811B0A333D8.description: Students will demonstrate critical thinking skills to analyze and evaluate dance.

6F2196CC919F4ACF88A46307F039ACC6.description: Recognize how self-assessment can be used to refine dance performance (e.g., maintain a dance journal, use research, resources, notation, peer assessments, and self-reflections).
comments: Give a few minutes at the end of each class period for journaling.

879BEBF2442249A2A5882DEBFF3325EC.description: Identify the impact of performance values of clarity, concentration, focus, and projection on dance performance (e.g., collaborate with peers for group work using learned movement materials).
comments: Feedback from an informed outside source on performance values. Create an action plan on given feedback. Learn how to take constructive criticism.

357912345F7947F5BC8D79AB86FD62A3.description: Use appropriate behaviors and etiquette to observe, create, and perform dance movements (e.g., reflect upon personal criteria to evaluate dance, and share in class discussion).
comments: Use student self-reflection and peer assessment. Implement evaluation skills.

DDE9518AA82A42758E71DC3FE0EDB9B0.description: Students will understand how to use performance values kinesthetic awareness, concentration, focus, and etiquette to enhance dance performance.

E60CDAD7452048EB8F57AE06AF21758E.description: Implement technical skills from a variety of dance forms (e.g., modern, ballet, tap, jazz, hip-hop) after viewing a performance.
comments: Bring in a guest artist that specializes in a genre. View an outside performance and replicate the choreography.

13FB62916FC94BF2B4EFD4EF51A85155.description: Move in varied rhythms, explore spatial orientations, and connect a series of dance moves with differing intentions as dictated by style, genre, or other influences (e.g., use rhythm, space, weight, flow to respond to various influences).
comments: Connect step series and perform with differing intentions apropos to the style of outside influences.
Explore basic steps from a teacher-created list of dance forms. Teacher models and student demonstrates.
31F307E5962C4364B7D89A0C06D68B8C.description: Execute body movements with flexibility, endurance, strength, and accuracy to develop dance technique (e.g., execute movement in a variety of dance forms with accuracy).

D3380BDA436940CAA6713083928F7943.description: Students will comprehend and demonstrate movement skills in dance.

BB7A1EF7EEF94BBB8F74E07567D48157.description: Manipulate movement ideas and choose from a variety of solutions to movement problems to establish a simple movement study with others (e.g., collaborate with peers to set formations and spatial patterns for a group work using learned movement material).
comments: *Give students a beginning of a movement phrase and have them finish it as a group.

1FAC79097EF94EDEA3F5F9C764DB332C.description: Invent movement sequences with others, improvise to generate movement ideas that develop from a variety of prompts and sources (e.g., incorporate various ideas to combine and layer movement elements).
comments: *Respond to musical accents, rhythms, narratives, artwork, images.

E347C78990E441ED8F3353CDF48147D5.description: Create and compare multiple movement phrases that use a variety of dance elements and simple choreographic structures (e.g., deconstruct movement to explore choreographic structures).
comments: Explore what happens to a phrase when you change the tempo, level, direction, sequence, repetition.

09E21B1E4451433383CDD9C0E0D26E93.description: Generate spontaneous and exaggerated movement independently to construct ideas, images, feelings, and experiences (e.g., use a memory or personal narrative (glossary) to create a short movement phrase).
comments: Through movement, express a time you were scared.

BD750DC0C6194DFB8C4BB6A94A79964E.description: Students will use dance elements, choreographic principles, and structures to construct dances that communicate ideas, images, feelings, and experiences.

EE1488D38831408EB24A7D263A05DDEC.description: Students will develop knowledge and skills to create, perform, respond to, and connect artistic ideas and expressions through dance and movement.

document.title: Nebraska Mathematics Standards

DC3C9240CD22421B8951F7033C2B26A2.description: No additional indicator(s) at this level.

AB3FFFEDC7E24D228DA4CBCA9ADE4BD3.description: Probability: Students will interpret and apply concepts of probability.

0841373F0B1047DC970D0CF55681167C.description: Ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and compare categories by identifying how many more or less are in a particular category using a picture graph.

05409A6CE2624BAD8A9E8CB21796ACF3.description: Analysis & Applications: Students will analyze data to address the situation.

6F1D32CA8300406492115851536D2206.description: Organize and represent a data set with up to three categories using a picture graph.

2A5B4116605A404C84B03BBC75CC5922.description: Representations: Students will create displays that represent data.

7D4F15F48C3A48CC8A8FFBBD1F9F8F4C.description: Data: Students will communicate data analysis/probability concepts using multiple representations to reason, solve problems, and make connections within mathematics and across disciplines.

AE7569D7ACE14812A023DDAB4DC88446.description: Order three objects by directly comparing their lengths, or indirectly by using a third object.

07F23AD03C144D538223F41243D74AC4.description: Measure objects by using a shorter object end-to-end and know that the length of the object is the amount of same-size objects that span it lined up end-to-end.

EBE72A34A5784BCEAF306AC45B90C34E.description: Tell and write time to the half hour and hour using analog and digital clocks.

AEEDAA5F3ABC4C8CAADC032204FE4207.description: Identify, name, and understand the value of dimes and pennies (e.g., a dime is equal to ten pennies) relating to tens and ones, and solve real-world problems involving dimes and pennies, using ¢ symbol appropriately (e.g., If you have four dimes and two pennies, how many cents do you have?).

C3E4FA63568541FC9FEAB78994C27140.description: Measurement: Students will perform and compare measurements and apply formulas.

FC8CF6DE1900463AAD0C1380656B2443.description: No additional indicator(s) at this level. Mastery is expected at previous grade levels.

82038E835D2144359AD1110F7619C751.description: Coordinate Geometry: Students will determine location, orientation, and relationships on the coordinate plane.

73E556CA746E4B408740560CDC8A7CB8.description: Use two-dimensional shapes (e.g., rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) and three-dimensional shapes (e.g., cubes, rectangular prisms, cones, and cylinders) to compose and describe new shapes.

FB3A2299C8DF42A18F7E95959A3ABD62.description: Decompose circles and rectangles into two and four equal parts, using the terms "halves", "fourths" and "quarters", and use the phrases "half of", "fourths of", and "quarter of".

8B1E30B5CFFA44689807A0A060E8505A.description: Determine defining and non-defining attributes of two-dimensional shapes; build and draw shapes that match the given definition.

142C7BEB37A84426AAA2C492A4D77E71.description: Characteristics: Students will identify and describe geometric characteristics and create two- and three-dimensional shapes.

FC5BA52FB363405AA5B47F4B82FE13B1.description: Geometry: Students will communicate geometric concepts and measurement concepts using multiple representations to reason, solve problems, and make connections within mathematics and across disciplines.

A8F476F030AF4E6EAA5611C776CAC8A7.description: Create a real-world problem to represent a given equation involving addition and subtraction within 20.

270B5247AB91437C86647EEFA7C2A906.description: Solve real-world problems that include addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20 by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol to represent the unknown number in the problem.

FFA285F9E6E1440A8085D0C1744D7BC4.description: QUALITY ASSURANCE. Any contractor or provider of competency evaluations shall conduct a standard quality assurance program measuring elements of structure, process, and outcomes of all components of the nurse aide competency evaluation. Written and skills exams must be linked to the nurse aide job analysis and supported by psychometric data determining the validity of all testing items on an ongoing basis.

This includes a secure system for data management and transmission of data to the Department, as well as the maintenance and security of questions in the written and skills examination pool.

Any person who does not complete the evaluation satisfactorily will be advised in writing within 5 calendar days after the test is scored of the areas which the person did not pass and that the person has 3 opportunities to take the evaluation. The competency testing entity will inform the nurse aide registry of the nurse aide’s scores within 14 calendar days after the test is completed.

Skilled nursing facilities that participate in Medicare and nursing facilities that participate in Medicaid are not eligible to administer and evaluate competency evaluations. A nurse aide course instructor cannot teach a student in the nurse aide course and administer the competency evaluation to the same student. Such facilities must apply for approval in accordance with this chapter, but need not submit curriculum materials required by this chapter except to the extent that the course will vary in any manner from the approved course. Applicants must indicate on the application the title of the approved course to be used, name of the entity whose approved course will be used, and the date on which such course was approved.

Stat. § 71-6039 except Intermediate Care Facilities for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF/IID) must be given by a single sponsor or organization and include, at a minimum, 75 clock hours of instruction, including at least 16 hours of supervised practical training. In addition, the course must include at least 1 hour of instruction on the responsibility of each nurse aide to report suspected abuse or neglect at a minimum, the curriculum must include:

42EFA17F5A42455183C9987723995FE6.description: DISCIPLINARY ACTION. A nursing home is subject to disciplinary action against its license under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 71-6042 or this chapter.

8FA4D76F706B410391A623EA16B7008F.description: WRITTEN NOTICE. Nurse aides will be notified in writing of a finding of conviction.

0F0F3F0CD90C4F78804E59C019B592D2.description: FINDINGS OF CONVICTION. The Department will document convictions of crimes involving moral turpitude rationally related to the practice of a nurse aide by placing a finding of conviction on the Nurse Aide Registry.

CAF2EFE5958344B4BCF403DDD1F14C0C.description: Successfully complete a competency evaluation as described in 172 NAC 108-006.

AA30B2EB4F15499296FF4A1DAE27333C.description: Demonstrate at least the minimum acceptable proficiency in tasks or duties connected with each skill in the curriculum prescribed in 172 NAC 108-004, as determined by the registered nurse administering the course and the course instructor; and

39B647219ABD4ABBB4982BF91E66DD5A.description: Successfully complete a Department-approved training program;

ABB4961A0320447EB19BACB3C617C0A4.description: PRACTICE. To act as a nurse aide, individuals must meet the requirements of Neb. Rev. Stat. § 71-6039 and the following:

07B548D421AF4AD48AB9A99B10A0FE76.description: RESIDENT. Any person domiciled, residing, or receiving care and treatment, for a period in excess of 24 hours, in a nursing home.

BCB0D05F848F4136B458215607B6FA1E.description: PROGRAM OR COURSE. The terms program and course are used synonymously in these regulations. The Nurse Aide Training Program consists of one course.

37CEA8316FE0477BA7D8132A293DE45E.description: NURSE AIDE REGISTRY. The central data bank of individuals eligible to function as nurse aides in certified facilities established by 471 Nebraska Administrative Code (NAC) 12.

4C30F6C9B6064C71B682EA4AA8FC9D6F.description: CURRICULUM. A detailed outline, description, or syllabus submitted to the Department as part of the course approval process by an association, hospital, nursing home, educational institution, or health care facility sponsoring a nurse aide training program.

B25750BAA14940F6B885741DBE69F234.description: ADMINISTRATOR. The operating officer for the health care facility, regardless of whether titled as administrator, manager, superintendent, director, or with a similar designation. The administrator of a licensed intermediate care facility, nursing facility, skilled nursing facility, or intermediate care facility for individuals with intellectual disabilities must be licensed by the State of Nebraska.

9ECA8C4E61B341A3B3FB3C39B5DE52AA.description: DEFINITIONS. Definitions are found in Neb. Rev. Stat. § 71-6038 and this chapter.

26B6FF0831B940A1B0B6976061F6F4CD.description: SCOPE AND AUTHORITY. These regulations govern the qualifications and training requirements for nurse aides employed in nursing homes. Statutory authority for this chapter is Nebraska Revised Statutes (Neb. Rev. Stat.) §§ 71-6038, 71-6039, and 71-6040 to 71-6042. These regulations are consistent with federal requirements at 42 CFR § 483, Subpart D, as it existed on the effective date of these regulations.
